item.title: Political Science Instructors Open Pool 2026
item.description: Job Description Position Summary: This is an open pool for adjunct instructors in the Political Science department a Colorado State University. The Department will review applications for instructors to teach undergraduate courses on an as-needed basis throughout the year. When positions become available, they may be offered 4.5-mos or 9-mos academic appointments and may include an option for summer teaching. Positions needed may be for both online or in-person classes. Please apply knowing that in-person teaching maybe required. Salary is dependent on degree type, teaching load, and service expectations. Description of Work Unit: The Department of Political Science at Colorado State University provides quality undergraduate and graduate educational programs to enhance students’ knowledge about government, politics and public affairs. Our curriculum covers the breadth of the Political Science discipline including American politics, comparative politics, international relations, political theory, and public policy and administration with an additional and unique specialization in environmental politics and policy. Our students develop strong critical thinking and analytical skills and learn to effectively communicate complex ideas. Our faculty and graduate students conduct research to advance knowledge about government and politics and to identify solutions to societal problems in the United States and around the world. Founded in 1870, Colorado State University is among the nation’s leading research universities and enrolls approximately 32,000 undergraduate, graduate, and professional students. Located an hour north of the Denver metro area, Fort Collins is a vibrant community of approximately 157,000 residents that offers the convenience of a small town with all the amenities of a large city. Fort Collins is situated on the Front Range of the Rocky Mountains with views of 14,000 foot peaks, and offers access to numerous cultural, recreational, and outdoor opportunities. Salary Range: $46,000 - $50,000 Essential Job Duties: The essential job duties will be teaching, which may include: Preparing lectures Creating assignments Holding office hours Grading course materials Conditions of Employment: Pre-employment criminal background check (required for new hires). Supervision: This position reports to the Department Chair of Political Science. Minimum Qualifications: Preferred Qualifications: Application Instructions: This is an open pool posting. Applications will be reviewed as hiring needs arise, and qualified applicants may be contacted by individual faculty members if a suitable opportunity becomes available. To apply, please upload the following documents: 1. Cover Letter 2. Current Resume or CV 3. A copy of Unofficial Transcripts (optional) This open pool that expires at 11:59 PM on December 31, 2026. Applicants wishing to be considered after this date must reapply. Please note, applicants may redact information from their application materials that identifies their age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. Employee Benefits Colorado State University is not just a workplace; it’s a thriving community that’s transforming lives and improving the human condition through world-class teaching, research, and service. With a robust benefits package, collaborative atmosphere, and focus on work-life balance, CSU is where you can thrive, grow, and make a lasting impact. Background Check Policy Statement Colorado State University strives to provide a safe study, work, and living environment for its faculty, staff, volunteers and students. To support this environment and comply with applicable laws and regulations, CSU conducts background checks for the finalist before a final offer. The type of background check conducted varies by position and can include, but is not limited to, criminal history, sex offender registry, motor vehicle history, financial history, and/or education verification. Background checks will also be conducted when required by law or contract and when, in the discretion of the University, it is reasonable and prudent to do so. EEO Colorado State University (CSU) provides equal employment opportunities to all applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

item.title: Campaign Organizer Help Defeat Pete Ricketts And Flip The Senate
item.description: Campaign Organizer- Nebraska Location and Timeline: We are hiring a full-time Campaign Organizer to begin by the end of August and continue through Election Day. The locations are Scottsbluff, North Platte, Grand Island, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk. This will expand over the program, so if you are a Nebraskan who lives further away or willing to relocate, please still apply! Who We Are: The Outreach Team is the national engine of campaigners and organizers building a fairer, cleaner, safer, and more peaceful world. We invest in people at every level with industry-leading pay/benefits, rigorous training and support and real paths to leadership. General Overview: Neighbor, it’s your time to step up for Nebraska. We need your love for our state and its people, your skills earned from years of hard work, and your ability to connect with other Nebraskans. Frankly, it’s the only way we are going to pry back our government and economy from the billionaires who have taken over. The good news is that there are more of us than there are of them. We just need to harness our power… conversation by conversation, on every porch, corner, driveway, sidewalk, field, and farm in Nebraska. And we need you to lead the charge. Join us on behalf of the Working Class Majority Pac. We are looking for Organizers to talk to voters about Dan Osborn’s run for Senate in Nebraska’s upcoming election. If you believe that real political power is built from the ground up through deep organizing and face-to-face conversations, we want you on our team in Scottsbluff, North Platte, Grand Island, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk. Organizers will be charged with recruiting, training, and working with a team of volunteers in key counties in Nebraska. The Organizer will start by building and recruiting a team of supporters and volunteers around canvassing. From there, Organizers will continue to engage volunteers through a series of campaign events and actions. Requirements: Valid driver's license and Insurance as well as a verifiable record of safe driving. Must be over 21 (in order to drive the rental car if needed) Must be available full-time. What You'll Do: Recruit and Train a Community of Volunteer Activists Call and text supporters and recruit them into grassroots actions. Identify new supporters and volunteers by knocking doors, gathering petitions, flyering, and conducting in-field recruitment efforts in the community and on local campuses. Run grassroots skills training to develop effective campaigners among volunteers. Keep meticulous track of a volunteer list so that no potential volunteer falls through the cracks. Represent the campaign through participation in community spaces and events, while engaging and uplifting coalition and partner organizations. Generate Campaign Actions Gather over a thousand petitions from the community in support of key campaign issues. Recruit and train volunteers to generate more petitions and volunteer engagement at events. Recruit and engage with community leaders, organizational partners, and VIPs to build meaningful relationships while generating new supporters, volunteers, and event attendees. Organize High-Volume Visibility Events Organize and execute exciting, high-visibility in-person events demonstrating support for working families in Nebraska. Educate community members about constituents around affordability and action opportunities and the urgency of continued actions. Nail 100% of all messaging and legal requirements and ensure that volunteers do the same. Manage Digital Campaign, Data Management, and Reporting Tools Demonstrate public support by recruiting volunteers to post on their own social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. Use peer-to-peer texting services and relational organizing tools to communicate with community members. Write and send timely and compelling email campaigns to recruit activists to campaign activities. Track every interaction with detailed notes in order to report numbers daily and write weekly reports on the results of the campaign. Who You Are & Keys to Success (the must-haves): To be successful in this job, you will excel in these areas: Relationship Building: You develop and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with a diverse group of local and statewide community members. You are attentive and empathetic to the communities we serve, regardless of race, ethnicity, class, gender, or ability, and can identify shared values across communities for collective growth. You can build authentic relationships through authenticity and reliability, continuously uplifting others and their goals. You are comfortable and experienced in public speaking to a group about constituents around affordability and action opportunities. Inclusive and Collaborative Leadership: You approach leadership with a "power with" mindset that recognizes the impact power hierarchies have in different settings. You can learn from others, see and hear other perspectives, and step in or step back as necessary. You are reliable and accountable, always transparent about your abilities, capacities, and expectations. You honor the time and commitments of others while inspiring them to meet goals. Commitment to Equity and Inclusion: You have a proven ability to develop meaningful connections with diverse communities, including a wide range of community organizations, community leaders, and community members. You work with the community and within the workplace to identify areas of improvement for a more equitable environment. You take continued action and efforts to improve your REI knowledge, skills, and tools. Drive to Achieve Results: You have experience accomplishing ambitious goals and getting results, even when there are obstacles. You have the experience or ability to plan backwards to meet multiple goals timely and effectively. When there are unexpected changes, you bounce back and adjust quickly, learning and improving from any mistakes. Skills and Experiences we Expect of all Outreach Team employees: Commitment to equity and justice. Experience bringing a lens of inclusivity to all of your interactions with colleagues and community members. Passion for the role that your work plays in creating change in the world. Kindness and consideration for others. Drive to work collaboratively: learning from others; stepping-in or stepping-back when needed. Transparency: comfort admitting what you do and don't know, your capacity, and abilities. Task management: Able to adapt to the evolving needs of a project. Able to tackle big-picture projects and break them down into smaller pieces. Organized and efficient: Experience or demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects or goals at once in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Acute attention to detail: Track interactions and tasks with detailed notes. Plans ahead for roadblocks and bounces back quickly when problems arise. Effective communication skills (written or spoken) that are clear, concise and honest. Comfortable and excited to speak about the campaign publicly. Coach and learning mentality: successful experience or willingness to learn new things and pick up new skills on the job. Able to learn from mistakes and try again. Understanding of how your words and actions affect others, including an awareness of power language and communication accessibility. Ability to work weekends and weekday evenings, occasional holidays. Nice-to-Haves, but Not Required: Organizing experience in or around Grand Island, North Platte, Scottsbluff, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk Nebraska. Experience working for nonprofits and issue campaigns. Data Management and Evaluation Experience: Experience working with various data management systems and tools, mainly Google Suite. Experience with Relevant Campaign Tools and Technologies: VAN, Action Network, ThruText, MailChimp, eCRMs like EveryAction, or social media tools (Twitter, Facebook, Instagram). Event or Project Planning & Management, Implementation or Evaluation. Knowledge or previous experience working in roles that support constituents around affordability and action opportunities is a plus If you were here right now, you would be: Recruiting, training and developing activist leaders in your community to collect supporter petitions, educate others on key campaign issues, and recruit constituents to in-district events and actions. Planning and executing events for constituents around affordability as well as action opportunities including, but not limited to: door knocking, phonebanking, petitioning, visibility events, educational events, and more. Developing relationships with community leaders on corporate accountability, health care, and justice Engaging and expanding our support network through public visibility actions, voter outreach, and relationship-building. Salary, Benefits and Perks: The salary for this position is $55,000 to $67,000 for full-time. We offer a generous benefits package, including paid vacation and sick leave, health insurance, and hands-on training. At the end of the campaign, there may be opportunities for advancement and bonuses. At The Outreach Team, we prioritize equity and inclusion. We are an equal opportunity employer and we strongly encourage Black, indigenous, people of color, women, people with previous felony convictions, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and others who identify with underrepresented groups to apply. To Apply: Visit: https://theoutreachteam.applytojob.com/apply

Generate Campaign Actions Gather over a thousand petitions from the community in support of key campaign issues. Recruit and train volunteers to generate more petitions and volunteer engagement at events. Recruit and engage with community leaders, organizational partners, and VIPs to build meaningful relationships while generating new supporters, volunteers, and event attendees. Organize High-Volume Visibility Events Organize and execute exciting, high-visibility in-person events demonstrating support for working families in Nebraska. Educate community members about constituents around affordability and action opportunities and the urgency of continued actions. Nail 100% of all messaging and legal requirements and ensure that volunteers do the same. Manage Digital Campaign, Data Management, and Reporting Tools Demonstrate public support by recruiting volunteers to post on their own social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. Use peer-to-peer texting services and relational organizing tools to communicate with community members. Write and send timely and compelling email campaigns to recruit activists to campaign activities. Track every interaction with detailed notes in order to report numbers daily and write weekly reports on the results of the campaign. Who You Are & Keys to Success (the must-haves): To be successful in this job, you will excel in these areas: Relationship Building: You develop and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with a diverse group of local and statewide community members. You are attentive and empathetic to the communities we serve, regardless of race, ethnicity, class, gender, or ability, and can identify shared values across communities for collective growth. You can build authentic relationships through authenticity and reliability, continuously uplifting others and their goals. You are comfortable and experienced in public speaking to a group about constituents around affordability and action opportunities. Inclusive and Collaborative Leadership: You approach leadership with a "power with" mindset that recognizes the impact power hierarchies have in different settings. You can learn from others, see and hear other perspectives, and step in or step back as necessary. You are reliable and accountable, always transparent about your abilities, capacities, and expectations. You honor the time and commitments of others while inspiring them to meet goals. Commitment to Equity and Inclusion: You have a proven ability to develop meaningful connections with diverse communities, including a wide range of community organizations, community leaders, and community members. You work with the community and within the workplace to identify areas of improvement for a more equitable environment. You take continued action and efforts to improve your REI knowledge, skills, and tools. Drive to Achieve Results: You have experience accomplishing ambitious goals and getting results, even when there are obstacles. You have the experience or ability to plan backwards to meet multiple goals timely and effectively. When there are unexpected changes, you bounce back and adjust quickly, learning and improving from any mistakes. Skills and Experiences we Expect of all Outreach Team employees: Commitment to equity and justice. Experience bringing a lens of inclusivity to all of your interactions with colleagues and community members. Passion for the role that your work plays in creating change in the world. Kindness and consideration for others. Drive to work collaboratively: learning from others; stepping-in or stepping-back when needed. Transparency: comfort admitting what you do and don't know, your capacity, and abilities. Task management: Able to adapt to the evolving needs of a project. Able to tackle big-picture projects and break them down into smaller pieces. Organized and efficient: Experience or demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects or goals at once in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Acute attention to detail: Track interactions and tasks with detailed notes. Plans ahead for roadblocks and bounces back quickly when problems arise. Effective communication skills (written or spoken) that are clear, concise and honest. Comfortable and excited to speak about the campaign publicly. Coach and learning mentality: successful experience or willingness to learn new things and pick up new skills on the job. Able to learn from mistakes and try again. Understanding of how your words and actions affect others, including an awareness of power language and communication accessibility. Ability to work weekends and weekday evenings, occasional holidays. Nice-to-Haves, but Not Required: Organizing experience in or around Grand Island, North Platte, Scottsbluff, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk Nebraska. Experience working for nonprofits and issue campaigns. Data Management and Evaluation Experience: Experience working with various data management systems and tools, mainly Google Suite. Experience with Relevant Campaign Tools and Technologies: VAN, Action Network, ThruText, MailChimp, eCRMs like EveryAction, or social media tools (Twitter, Facebook, Instagram). Event or Project Planning & Management, Implementation or Evaluation. Knowledge or previous experience working in roles that support constituents around affordability and action opportunities is a plus If you were here right now, you would be: Recruiting, training and developing activist leaders in your community to collect supporter petitions, educate others on key campaign issues, and recruit constituents to in-district events and actions. Planning and executing events for constituents around affordability as well as action opportunities including, but not limited to: door knocking, phonebanking, petitioning, visibility events, educational events, and more. Developing relationships with community leaders on corporate accountability, health care, and justice Engaging and expanding our support network through public visibility actions, voter outreach, and relationship-building. Salary, Benefits and Perks: The salary for this position is $55,000 to $67,000 for full-time. We offer a generous benefits package, including paid vacation and sick leave, health insurance, and hands-on training. At the end of the campaign, there may be opportunities for advancement and bonuses. At The Outreach Team, we prioritize equity and inclusion. We are an equal opportunity employer and we strongly encourage Black, indigenous, people of color, women, people with previous felony convictions, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and others who identify with underrepresented groups to apply. To Apply: Visit: https://theoutreachteam.applytojob.com/apply

item.title: Senior Government Affairs Manager
item.description: Overview The Washington State and Global Employee Engagement (WSGEE) team is seeking a Senior Government Affairs Manager to work in a fast-paced environment to provide programmatic support, policy and advocacy strategy execution, government affairs outreach, and project management. This individual will be a critical member of the team, working cross-functionally across our government, community, and employee engagement teams to support our home state and the Cascadia region (WA, OR, BC) as a whole. The position will work closely with the Senior Director of Government Affairs, as well as other members of the WSGEE team, providing political and strategic analysis and recommendations that inform and execute our advocacy strategy, policy positioning, and relationship development. This opportunity will allow you to deepen and grow Microsoft’s partnerships and influence with elected and appointed officials with an emphasis on state and local officials across Washington state. You will play a key role in ensuring the government affairs team within WSGEE stays coordinated and aligned on policy positions and priority areas of work. In this role you will be a systems-thinker and proactive problem solver, creative, motivated, and personable, capable of building strong relationships and juggling multiple priorities, with a strong drive for results and commitment to excellence. You will research government affairs issues impacting business strategy and economic development, attend meetings and events, develop prep materials, and collaborate with internal teams on cross-team projects. Responsibilities Promote Microsoft as a critical force for good across issues that are imperative to a strong state economy in Washington and the Cascadia region, including housing, education, transportation, sustainability, and economic development, and a leader in technological innovation that helps people, governments and organizations achieve more. Represent Microsoft by attending, managing and coordinating events with elected and appointed officials, advocates, and other community leaders, which will involve developing content, drafting materials, and driving social media engagement. Collaborate with other teams to ensure a communications strategy is in place. Manage tracking and monitoring for policy-, industry-, or geographical-related issues and execute on Microsoft strategies and/or programs related to government affairs. Respond to issues by engaging relevant parties, prioritizing issues, sharing political intelligence, and escalating matters or contacting a subject matter experts, as appropriate. Contribute to the formation of Microsoft’s policy agenda, advocacy strategies, community relations, and/or business objectives across the company. Gather and integrate data and intelligence to support the preparation of advocacy materials, internal and external briefings, and other documentation. Lead, coordinate, and gain buy-in for intra- and cross-group projects, working with others to resolve conflicts and ensuring team alignment. Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to understand and align objectives, priorities, and resources. Qualifications Required/minimum qualifications Bachelor's Degree in Public Policy, Public Administration, Political Science, Business Administration, Technology, Law, Liberal Arts, Engineering, or related field AND 4+ years work experience in government affairs, corporate affairs, public policy, government, or related area OR equivalent experience. Additional or preferred qualifications 3+ years experience in developing and managing strategic relationships to advocate and influence public, regulatory, and technology policy priorities. 3+ years experience influencing, developing, or supporting public policy or political campaigns. Government Affairs IC4 - The typical base pay range for this role across the U.S. is USD $105,800 - $204,000 per year. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $138,400 - $223,300 per year. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here: https://careers.microsoft.com/us/en/us-corporate-pay This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. If you need assistance with religious accommodations and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application process, read more about requesting accommodations.

item.title: Political Reporter Editor
item.description: If you love to follow politics and tell the stories of election campaigns, parties, and voters, we might be looking for you. Iowa Public Radio is hiring a political reporter-editor in our Des Moines newsroom. You’ll report on state politics for our broadcast and digital platforms and lead our coverage of the Iowa caucuses. In 2028, Iowa will once again kick off the Republican presidential nominating process. You’ll also work with IPR news managers to coordinate our election coverage strategy, guide other IPR reporters in their work on political stories, and help plan our election night coverage. This position is based in Des Moines, Iowa’s largest city and part of the fastest-growing metro area in the Midwest. There are lots of places to catch a concert, enjoy a great meal, watch a game, or bike for miles on one of the area’s many trails. Our ideal candidate is curious, motivated, and has a deep interest in the issues that affect people throughout Iowa. We’re looking for someone with strong editorial judgment and the ability to write quickly and clearly, while telling a good story. If you’re passionate about impactful journalism, care about ethics and diversity, can handle several things at once and are committed to making great radio, we’d love to hear from you. We know there are great candidates who might not exactly fit into what we’ve described here or who have important skills we haven’t listed. If that sounds like you, don’t hesitate to apply and tell us about yourself. Iowa Public Radio is a well-respected and thriving non-profit organization. We offer an excellent benefits package, including health benefits, a retirement plan with a 2-to-1 employer match, immediate accrual of vacation (16 hours monthly) and sick (12 hours monthly) time and a flexible work environment. ANTICIPATED HIRING RANGE : $56,000 - $71,000 SUMMARY : The Political Reporter & Editor serves as Iowa Public Radio’s lead political reporter, covering races for major statewide and federal offices, including the presidential caucus cycle. This person will help coordinate IPR’s wider coverage of political campaigns and races, and assist in editing IPR reporters’ political reporting. This position will also be responsible for coordination and production of special political projects ranging from stories to podcasts. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Five years of experience working in a professional journalism environment An understanding of local, state and federal political systems Experience working in multimedia platforms, including photographs, video and web platforms Experience operating a variety of broadcast equipment including audio boards, digital editing systems (e.g. Adobe Audition), field recording units, and other production equipment A valid state-issued driver’s license and reliable transportation. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Three years of experience in political reporting An eye for diverse voices and sources in stories Strong writing skills and experience editing the work of other reporters Experience as a public radio reporter and/or host Firm foundation in journalism ethics, news gathering, and reporting techniques APPLICATION PROCESS : Apply through the position link on the IPR website . For full consideration, applications must include the following: A detailed resume . A narrative carefully detailing how your experience compares to the job duties and qualifications listed for this position. The narrative should not exceed two pages. Sample(s) of your work: Writing samples that include spot news and a news-oriented feature. Online content you have produced (please send links). Online content can be a web build-out of a radio story or news content that was designed to be web-only. Please do not send stories you have produced with the help of a national network. Demo containing one newscast-length story (spot), and one feature-length report (3:00-5:00) that you have edited and produced. If you have one, we’d love to hear a sample of a two-way you did with a program host, or an interview you’ve conducted for a podcast or other audio production. Please upload the demo to Soundcloud or another hosting site and send IPR links. Names and contact information, including email addresses, for three work references , including at least one supervisory reference Employment at Iowa Public Radio is dependent upon successful completion of a criminal background check including a driving record review and reference check. IPR will accept applications through 5:00 p.m. Friday, September 25, 2026 . OUR VALUES : Integrity : We maintain the highest standards of journalism, providing trustworthy and relevant content with meaningful context. Curiosity : We serve an inquisitive audience by asking questions, seeking knowledge, and exploring new ideas. Belonging : We strive to reflect Iowa’s cultural complexity by offering a supportive, equitable space for individuals and communities to tell the stories unique to their lived experiences. Respect : We create a culture of respect for our audience, sources, and staff. Innovation : We support creativity and embrace new ways of serving our audience. OUR COMMITMENT TO EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY : Iowa Public Radio is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Discrimination because of race, color, religion, national origin or sex is prohibited. If you believe you have been a victim of discrimination, please notify the appropriate local, state or federal agency.

item.title: Public Policy Researcher Entry Level Hybrid Summer 2027
item.description: Are you looking to work on current and emerging policy issues? Do you want to apply your education and experience to help government agencies improve the way they develop and implement regulations, policies, and programs? Our Regulatory, Policy, and Economics Portfolio has over 30 years of experience supporting the design, implementation, and improvement of federal programs for key clients including the Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Transportation, Department of Homeland Security, Department of Labor, Department of Interior, and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Join our multidisciplinary team of regulatory specialists, policy analysts, economists, and attorneys. We combine legal, policy, economic, and scientific research and analysis to solve unique public policy challenges through innovative, accurate, timely, and high-quality products and services. Our dynamic work environment involves working on multiple projects simultaneously, supporting a variety of federal clients, and providing a wide range of support services. This entry-level full-time position will be hybrid from our Reston, VA headquarters (preferred) or Waltham, MA office and is available starting Summer 2027. The anticipated pay for this position will be in the low $60K range. Job Responsibilities: Participating in short- and long-term engagements to support federal clients whose responsibilities are to develop policies and craft regulations that implement the desired policy, explain the rationale of the rulemaking to interested parties; and implement the regulatory requirements Supporting federal agency efforts to transparently manage and analyze public comments received on proposed agency rules Assist in drafting and editing documents related to federal agency rulemakings Immersing oneself rapidly in varied projects for multiple clients Providing verbal and written progress updates to project staff Synthesizing information from rulemaking documents, literature, and other technical reports Assist in developing recommendations through collecting and analyzing both qualitative and quantitative data Drafting reports and presentations Interacting with clients to discuss ICF’s analysis Basic Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in public policy, government, environmental science, natural or physical science, political science, or related subjects U.S. Citizenship is required per federal contract requirements Ability to obtain and maintain a government security clearance Preferred Qualifications: Understanding of the federal rulemaking process Ability to obtain and maintain a moderate-level government security clearance Strong analytical and organizational skills are essential Ability to prioritize and work on multiple projects under strict deadlines in a fast-paced environment Excellent written and oral communications skills Detail-oriented and team-oriented approach Proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint) and Adobe; and Time management strategies Bot and Third-Party Applications Please note that this application must be submitted directly by the applicant for consideration. Failure to do so may result in the application being excluded for consideration . Applicants needing an accommodation for disability or religious purposes in connection with the application process should contact Candidateaccommodation@icf.com for assistance. Working at ICF ICF is a global advisory and technology services provider, but we’re not your typical consultants. We combine unmatched expertise with cutting-edge technology to help clients solve their most complex challenges, navigate change, and shape the future. We can only solve the world's toughest challenges by building a workplace that allows everyone to thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer . Together, our employees are empowered to share their expertise and collaborate with others to achieve personal and professional goals. For more information, please read our EEO policy. We will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Reasonable Accommodations are available, including, but not limited to, for disabled veterans, individuals with disabilities, and individuals with sincerely held religious beliefs, in all phases of the application and employment process. To request an accommodation, please email Candidateaccommodation@icf.com and we will be happy to assist . All information you provide will be kept confidential and will be used only to the extent to provide needed reasonable accommodations. Candidate AI Usage Policy At ICF, we are committed to ensuring a fair interview process for all candidates based on their own skills and knowledge. As part of this commitment, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to generate or assist with responses during interviews (whether in-person or virtual) is not permitted . This policy is in place to maintain the integrity and authenticity of the interview process. However, we understand that some candidates may require accommodation that involves the use of AI. If such an accommodation is needed, candidates are instructed to contact us in advance at candidateaccommodation@icf.com . We are dedicated to providing the necessary support to ensure that all candidates have an equal opportunity to succeed. Pay Range - There are multiple factors that are considered in determining final pay for a position, including, but not limited to, relevant work experience, skills, certifications and competencies that align to the specified role, geographic location, education and certifications as well as contract provisions regarding labor categories that are specific to the position. The pay range for this position based on full-time employment is : $50,386.00 - $85,656.00 Reston, VA (VA30)

item.title: Congressional Liaison Officer N2701
item.description: Position is 100% Onsite Who We Are : Founded in 2007, SimIS Inc. is an innovative information technology solution Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) that models future environments, requirements, and capabilities, and then secures the enterprise from internal and external threats compliant with Federal, State, and industry standard governance to ensure client mission success. Our performance standard is “excellence,” with an outcomes-based, quality focus in our services and products, guided by our core values of honesty (in word and deed), relationships (confidence and trust with clients and partners), teamwork (shared goals, mission, and purpose), loyalty (allegiance to our client and team), and importance of others (work and win as a team). SimIS is currently recruiting for the listed position and is contingent upon award. The position is anticipated to be “on site.” Job Description: SimIS, Inc. is seeking provides support for the role of Liaison Officer to the U.S. Congress to serve as our customers forward presence in Washington, D.C., representing interests, monitoring legislative dynamics, and cultivating strong relationships with Members of Congress, staffers, and relevant committees. SimIS, Inc. seeks a Congressional Liaison Officer to ensure our customers visibility on Capitol Hill, strengthening their network within the U.S. legislative branch, and supporting efforts to anticipate and adapt to U.S. defense priorities. Qualifications: Master's degree in Political Science, International Relations, Economics, Law, or a similar field. BS degree with significant Congressional staff experience will be considered. Five years of experience working with or within the U.S. Congress, particularly on defense, appropriations, and foreign policy issues. In-depth knowledge of the U.S. Congressional process, including authorization and appropriations cycles. A proven track record of success in a government relations position, with a demonstrated ability to manage a legislative portfolio, understand and communicate complex policies, and successfully navigate the legislative process. Excellent communication skills, particularly the ability to interface effectively with elected officials, policymakers, and key Congressional and federal staff, verbally, in writing, and through professional interpersonal skills, to inform, educate, and persuade in support of defense initiatives. Ability to work and communicate with colleagues across departments to gather the resources, skills, and expertise necessary to convey the customers message on Capitol Hill and across administrations. Ability to represent and advocate the organization's policy positions to Congress, the Executive Branch, think tanks, and other relevant stakeholders. Ability to develop and implement long- and short-term action plans that lead to the accomplishment of initiatives on innovation, capability development, and other assigned topics. Responsibilities: Monitor and analyze the U.S. defense budget process, from planning to execution, highlighting implications for NATO. Track ongoing Congressional defense reforms and assess their impact on NATO transformation. Provide strategic reporting on Congressional debates and decisions concerning Ukraine and broader Euro-Atlantic security. Assess budget issues linked to the U.S. troop presence in Europe, with specific attention to burden-sharing debates. Analyse the political dynamics of defense-related legislation, identifying key influencers and agendas. Plan and conduct informal engagements, including dinners and meetings, with legislators and staffers to promote ACT visibility. Monitor legislative initiatives, hearings, and committee activities relevant to NATO. Manage relationships with Members of Congress and provide tailored briefings on ACT and NATO priorities. Coordinate with U.S. executive agencies, NATO missions, and Allied embassies to ensure message coherence. Produce regular reports for SACT and POLAD on Congressional trends, risks, and opportunities.. Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision Short-Term Disability (at no cost to you) & Long-Term Disability Life Insurance 401(k) Savings Plan Flex Spending Accounts Tuition Assistance Program Professional Development Paid Time Off (PTO) 11 Federal Holidays each year SimIS, Inc. is an EOE / M / F / Disability / VET / Drug Free Employer

item.title: Director Government Affairs
item.description: Position Summary The Director will develop and maintain strong relationships with Members of Congress and congressional staff and advocate for CTA’s policy priorities across a broad range of issues affecting the consumer technology industry. The Director will serve as a key member of CTA’s federal lobbying team, working across the organization’s policy portfolio and helping identify opportunities to advance CTA’s policy priorities on Capitol Hill. The Director will also lead CTA’s federal policy and regulatory work on transportation and mobility, including autonomous vehicles and emerging transportation technologies. Key Responsibilities Primary: Build and maintain relationships with Members of Congress and congressional staff across both the House and Senate and serve as a key democratic relationship lead for CTA on Capitol Hill. Lead or co-lead CTA policy development and member working groups within the transportation portfolio. Lead CTA’s federal policy and regulatory engagement on transportation, mobility, autonomous vehicles, and related emerging technologies. Advocate for CTA’s legislative and policy priorities across the organization’s broader technology agenda. Identify opportunities to advance CTA priorities through legislation, congressional engagement, coalition activity, and political relationship-building. Prepare statements, testimony, talking points, briefing materials, and other advocacy materials for congressional engagement. Draft and submit comments to federal regulatory agencies on transportation and mobility issues. Organize and participate in congressional meetings, lobbying days, political events, policy briefings, technology demonstrations, and CES. Represent CTA before policymakers and at industry meetings, policy events, panels, and, as appropriate, in the press. Work closely with CTAPAC to develop and strengthen relationships with current and emerging technology leaders in Congress. Additional: Monitor congressional activity and identify legislative and political developments affecting CTA and its members. Liaise with industry coalitions and outside stakeholders, particularly on transportation and mobility issues. Support CTA thought leadership through articles, position papers, blogs, and other policy communications. Support CTA engagement on state and local transportation issues as appropriate. Provide member companies with relevant updates on congressional hearings, agency actions, and other policy developments. Support federal lobbying efforts outside the Director’s primary policy portfolio as needed. Perform other duties as required by business needs. Qualifications Work Experience: At least 6–8 years of experience in federal government affairs, congressional affairs, or public policy. Significant experience working in or with the U.S. Congress. Demonstrated experience building and maintaining relationships with Members of Congress and senior congressional staff. Experience with transportation, mobility, autonomous vehicles, or technology policy strongly preferred. Experience researching, analyzing, and communicating legislative and regulatory issues. Skills/Capabilities/Technical: Strong understanding of Congress, the legislative process, and the federal political environment. Excellent political judgment and ability to identify opportunities to advance organizational priorities. Exceptional relationship-building skills and the ability to develop, maintain, and leverage internal and external relationships. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work effectively across multiple policy areas and respond quickly to changing legislative priorities. Education/Trainings: Bachelor’s degree in political science or related field preferred, or commensurate experience. Additional Information: Must have flexibility to attend industry events in the early morning and evenings, and occasional weekends. Some travel required. About CTA Want to work at the forefront of innovation and make an impact across the technology industry? The Consumer Technology Association (CTA)® is the leading voice of the technology industry, representing innovators and shaping the future through advocacy, insights, and global events like CES®. When you join CTA, you become part of a team that values collaboration, transparency, and meaningful impact. At CTA, our culture is built by our people. We are: Staff-Focused – We value every voice and seek input across teams Transparent & Collaborative – We foster open communication and teamwork Open & Honest – We encourage thoughtful feedback, open dialogue, and continuous growth. Impact-Driven – We focus on work that drives meaningful results Adaptable & Forward-Thinking – We embrace innovation and change CTA has been recognized for its strong workplace culture, including honors such as the CARE Award (for 16 consecutive years), Washingtonian Best Places to Work, and the Cigna Healthy Workforce Designation (Gold Level). Compensation & Benefits CTA is committed to transparency and equitable pay practices. The anticipated salary range for this position is $170,000 – $180,000 , with final compensation determined based on experience, skills, and internal equity. This role may be eligible for bonus or additional compensation, where applicable. CTA offers a comprehensive benefits package supporting your health, financial well-being, and work-life balance, including: Health & Wellness – Medical, dental, and vision coverage with telemedicine access, wellness programs, and an on-site fitness center Financial Benefits – 401(k) with 100% employer match up to 6%, student loan assistance, and commuter benefits. Unique to CTA — a mortgage assistance program that may include eligibility for a forgivable home purchase loan of up to $40,000. Time Off & Flexibility – Paid time off, holidays, paid parental leave, and a hybrid work environment with flexible scheduling options Family & Lifestyle Support – Fertility and adoption assistance Professional Growth – Tuition reimbursement and ongoing professional development opportunities For more information about CTA’s benefits and total rewards offerings, please review our Benefits Guide. Equal Opportunity Employer Statement CTA is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. Applicant Data Privacy Notice CTA respects your privacy. Information collected during the application process will be used solely for recruitment purposes and handled in accordance with applicable data protection laws. By applying, you acknowledge CTA may retain your information for current and future opportunities. For more information, please review our Privacy Policy.

item.title: Director State Legislative Regulatory Affairs
item.description: Since opening our first self-storage facility in 1972, Public Storage has grown to become the largest owner and operator of self-storage facilities in the world. With thousands of locations across the U.S. and Europe, and more than 170 million net rentable square feet of real estate, we're also one of the largest landlords. We've been recognized as A Great Place to Work by the Great Place to Work Institute. And, our employees have also voted us as having Best Career Growth , ranked us in the Top 5% for Work Culture , and in the Top 10% for Diversity and Inclusion . We're a member of the S&P 500 and FT Global 500 . Our common and preferred stocks trade on the New York Stock Exchange. Public Storage is the nation’s leading self-storage provider, recognized for its iconic orange doors and commitment to delivering simple, reliable solutions to millions of customers across the country. We are expanding our creative team to enhance our consistent and engaging visual brand presence. The Director, State Legislative & Regulatory Affairs will monitor, assess, and help shape state and local policy developments affecting Public Storage and the self-storage industry. This role will serve as a strategic advisor to Legal, Compliance, Operations, Revenue Management, Marketing, Risk, and senior leadership on legislative and regulatory issues, with particular emphasis on consumer protection, pricing, advertising and marketing, lien laws, insurance, property operations, taxation, privacy, and other matters affecting a nationwide consumer-facing real estate business. The successful candidate will bring deep experience monitoring and managing legislative and regulatory activity across multiple states, translating complex developments into practical business guidance, and leading coordinated efforts among internal stakeholders, outside counsel, consultants, contract lobbyists, trade associations, and cross-functional teams nationwide. A law degree is not required; Public Storage is seeking a seasoned public policy, state government affairs, or regulatory affairs leader who can build scalable processes and manage a national portfolio of issues with sound judgment and executive presence. Key Responsibilities Monitor, analyze, and report on state and local legislative and regulatory developments affecting Public Storage, including proposed legislation, administrative rulemaking, attorney general activity, agency guidance, and emerging policy trends. Develop and manage a nationwide issue-tracking process that identifies risks and opportunities across multiple states and escalates priority matters to Legal, Compliance, Operations, and senior business leaders. Lead the coordination of state advocacy strategies, including developing policy positions, drafting testimony and comment letters, recommending legislative language, and supporting direct engagement with policymakers and regulators. Manage and coordinate external resources, including contract lobbyists, outside counsel, consultants, trade associations, and coalition partners, to ensure consistent strategy, timely intelligence, and effective execution across jurisdictions. Partner with internal stakeholders to assess the operational, financial, compliance, customer, and reputational impact of proposed laws and regulations and recommend practical response strategies. Translate complex legislative and regulatory developments into clear, actionable guidance for executives and business teams. Support regulatory and legislative strategies related to consumer protection, pricing, advertising and marketing, lien laws, insurance and risk, property operations, tax, privacy, call center practices, and other issues affecting the self-storage industry. Build and maintain relationships with state legislators, regulators, agency staff, attorneys general offices, governors’ offices, trade associations, business coalitions, and other external stakeholders. Prepare briefings, memoranda, issue summaries, talking points, testimony, correspondence, and executive-level reports on key legislative and regulatory matters. Track lobbying, political, gift, ethics, and disclosure obligations in partnership with Legal and Compliance to support adherence to applicable federal, state, and local requirements. Support integration and compliance planning for business expansion, acquisitions, entry into new jurisdictions, and changes in state operating requirements. Manage cross-functional workstreams and nationwide teams to ensure alignment, accountability, and timely execution on priority legislative and regulatory matters. 10–12+ years of relevant experience in state government affairs, legislative affairs, regulatory affairs, public policy, trade association advocacy, or a related role. Demonstrated experience monitoring, analyzing, and managing legislative and regulatory developments across multiple states. Proven ability to manage nationwide teams, external consultants, contract lobbyists, and cross-functional stakeholders in a matrixed environment. Strong understanding of state legislative and regulatory processes, including bill tracking, committee activity, rulemaking, public comment processes, coalition advocacy, and policymaker engagement. Experience developing advocacy strategies and translating policy developments into business, operational, and compliance recommendations. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to draft testimony, comment letters, policy briefs, executive summaries, and strategic recommendations. Strong project management skills, with the ability to prioritize competing issues, manage deadlines across jurisdictions, and create scalable systems for tracking and reporting. Sound judgment, discretion, and ability to advise senior leaders on sensitive, fast-moving, and high-impact public policy matters. Bachelor’s degree in political science, public policy, public administration, business, communications, or a related field required; advanced degree, public policy degree, or J.D. welcome but not required. Ability to travel regularly to state capitals, industry meetings, company locations, and external stakeholder engagements as needed. Preferred Experience Experience working for or with a national, multi-state, consumer-facing, real estate, retail, property management, financial services, logistics, or regulated services business. Experience managing issue portfolios involving consumer protection, pricing, advertising and marketing, contracts, lien laws, insurance, tax, privacy, or property operations. Familiarity with legislative tracking and government affairs platforms such as Quorum, FiscalNote, LexisNexis State Net, PolicyNote, or similar tools. Experience working with trade associations, coalitions, attorneys general offices, state regulatory agencies, and bipartisan policymaker networks. Experience building a legislative and regulatory affairs function, including processes for issue intake, tracking, escalation, stakeholder engagement, and executive reporting. Key Attributes Strategic, practical, and business-oriented approach to public policy and regulatory risk. Ability to operate independently while keeping internal stakeholders aligned and informed. Executive presence and credibility with senior leaders, policymakers, regulators, and external partners. Comfort managing ambiguity, competing priorities, and fast-moving legislative sessions across multiple jurisdictions. Collaborative style with the ability to lead through influence across legal, operational, compliance, and business teams. Public Storage is an equal opportunity employer and embraces diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other protected status. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply. **Sponsorship for Work Authorization is not available for this posting. Candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. without restrictions or requiring sponsorship now or in the future. We do not provide training plans or support for F-1 OPT, STEM OPT extensions, or future visa sponsorship.** REF4467F

item.title: Visiting Assistant Professor Of Political Science
item.description: Job Title Visiting Assistant Professor of Political Science Agency Texas A&M University - Corpus Christi Department College Of Liberal Arts Proposed Minimum Salary Commensurate Job Location Corpus Christi, Texas Job Type Faculty Job Description The College of Liberal Arts is seeking a Visiting Assistant Professor of Political Science in American Politics to begin in Fall 2027. The successful candidate will show excellent and enthusiastic teaching skills and demonstrate the ability to work in a team environment. Course assignments will be undergraduate courses across the Political Science curriculum. Teaching assignments may include classroom (face-to-face), hybrid, and online classes with various class sizes. Candidates should be prepared to teach core curriculum requirements such as American government and state and local government (emphasis on Texas). In addition, candidates will contribute to the teaching needs of the Political Science major including courses such as introduction to political science, Mexican American politics, research methods, and the senior capstone. The normal teaching load will be 4-4. The Department of Social Sciences (DSOC) is a multi-disciplinary department in the College of Liberal Arts that offers undergraduate degrees in Political Science and Criminal Justice and the graduate degree of Master of Public Administration. Through its contribution to the core curriculum, Political Science is one of the largest generators of student credit hours for the university. The Criminal Justice program is one of the largest undergraduate majors on campus. The MPA program is the second largest graduate program in the College of Liberal Arts. DSOC faculty are leaders on campus, in the community, and in their disciplines. We value excellence and work daily to support the University’s Islander Impact 2030 Overarching Goal to be nationally recognized for student success, academic achievement, research, creative activity, innovation, and service excellence. Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi is a vibrant, Hispanic and Minority Serving R2 Doctoral Research Institution that proudly provides a solid academic reputation, renowned faculty, and highly rated degree programs since 1947. The University has a heritage of teaching excellence with innovation in research and community engagement as part of the distinguished Texas A&M System. TAMU-CC is the only university in the nation located on its own island, at the heart of the Texas Gulf Coast. With palm tree lined pathways throughout the campus, nearby natural wetlands, a scenic hike-and-bike trail and pristine views of the beach and bays, Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi is a first-choice institution. Required Qualifications: Doctoral degree in Political Science or a closely related discipline from an accredited university. Advanced ABD will be considered; degree must be conferred at the time of appointment. Ability to teach courses in the Political Science program (including American government, state/Texas and local government, introduction to political science, research methods, and senior capstone). Ability to teach in a variety of formats and class sizes to include classroom, hybrid, and online courses. Commitment to excellence in teaching and student mentoring. TO APPLY : https://www.tamucc.edu/human-resources/careers/index.php All required documentation must be submitted to be considered for the position. A completed application will include: A letter of application addressing qualifications listed above including a teaching philosophy and/or evidence of excellence in teaching A curriculum vitae Three professional references including name, address, title, telephone number, and email addresses. Unofficial copies of graduate transcripts Application deadline: Sunday, November 1st, 2026 Position start date: Fall 2027 For questions about the position, please contact Dr. Isla Schuchs Carr, Department Chair, at isla.schuchscarr@tamucc.edu . NOTE: Employment may be impacted by the Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025 and the moratorium issued by Texas Governor Abbott on January 27, 2026. All positions are security-sensitive. Applicants are subject to a criminal history investigation, and employment is contingent upon the institution’s verification of credentials and/or other information required by the institution’s procedures, including the completion of the criminal history check. Equal Opportunity/Veterans/Disability Employer.

Graduation Date between December 2026 and July 2027 Major GPA of 3.0 Must be available to start immediately or no later than July 2026 Ability to work full time no later than July 2026 Proven analytical and problem-solving skills Demonstrated interpersonal and client relationships skills Demonstrated written and verbal communication skills Proven dedication to teamwork Proficiency in Microsoft Office, with focus on Word, PowerPoint and Excel Proven track record relevant to previous work experience About Kroll Join the global leader in risk and financial advisory solutions—Kroll. With a nearly century-long legacy, we blend trusted expertise with cutting-edge technology to navigate and redefine industry complexities. As a part of One Team, One Kroll, you'll contribute to a collaborative and empowering environment, propelling your career to new heights. Ready to build, protect, restore and maximize our clients’ value? Your journey begins with Kroll. item.title: Legislative Auditor Mid East Tennessee
item.description: Legislative Auditor: Mid-east Tennessee Location: Mid-east Tennessee (Putnam, Cumberland, White, Van Buren, Bledsoe, and Warren counties) Join us in our mission to make government work better. Role Snapshot This position conducts external audits for local government entities in the Mid-east Tennessee region, ensuring accountability, transparency, and effective operations across publicly funded organizations. Responsibilities may include examining and reviewing records, reports, financial statements, and management practices for state and local government entities and other organizations receiving public funds. Why You'll Love This Job Meaningful work that impacts communities across Tennessee Flexible schedules and a standard 37.5-hour workweek Opportunities for professional growth and development Collaborative and supportive team environment Comprehensive benefits and work-life balance What You'll Do Conduct audits of state and local governmental entities in accordance with professional auditing standards. Examine and review records, reports, financial statements, and management practices. Evaluate financial statement presentation, internal controls, compliance, and operational efficiency and effectiveness. Produce clear, logical, and well-supported workpapers and data analyses. Communicate clearly with auditees, coworkers, elected officials, and stakeholders. Take initiative, seek continuous improvement, and contribute to a collaborative team culture. What We're Looking For Required: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Business Administration with at least 24 semester hours in accounting Ability to learn quickly, think critically, problem solve, and produce accurate work Strong attention to detail and organizational skills Clear written and verbal communication skills Ability to work tactfully with coworkers, auditees, and stakeholders Sound judgment in evaluating situations and making decisions Preferred: Certified Public Accountant (CPA) license (not required but strongly encouraged for advancement) Experience in auditing, governmental accounting, or related fields Logistics Travel: For Local Government Auditors, travel is required but is generally confined to same day commutes to and from a job site. Overnight stays may be required, as necessary. Compensation: Competitive salary and benefits, including annual and sick leave, insurance plans, pension, 401(k), college fee waivers, and flexible schedules. About the Office The Office of the Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury audits state and local government entities and oversees financial and administrative management of state government. We are nationally recognized for professionalism and accountability and consistently rank as a Top Workplace. Learn more at www.comptroller.tn.gov Equal Opportunity Employer We are committed to fair and equal employment opportunities and maintaining a workplace free of discrimination and harassment. We prohibit discrimination based on race, color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, religion, disability, veteran status, or any category protected by law. NOTICE This position requires a criminal background check. You may be required to provide information about your criminal history to be considered for this position. Texting TOS and Privacy Policy: Message type: informational; you will receive text messages regarding your application and potentially regarding interview scheduling. You can cancel the SMS service at any time. Just text "STOP" to the short code. After you send the SMS message "STOP" to us, we will send you an SMS message to confirm that you have been unsubscribed. After this, you will no longer receive SMS messages from us. If you want to join again, just sign up as you did the first time and we will start sending SMS messages to you again. If you are experiencing issues with the messaging program, you can reply with the keyword HELP for more assistance, or you can get help directly at ig.askhr@cot.tn.gov . Message frequency will vary depending on the application process. Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages. Msg & data rates may apply. If you have any questions about your text plan or data plan, it is best to contact your wireless provider. If you have any questions regarding privacy, please read our privacy policy below. Privacy Policy: We collect your mobile number and related opt-in data for the delivery of SMS messages. Your mobile opt-in data and consent will not be shared with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.

item.title: Legislative And Regulatory Research Intern
item.description: At Fried Frank, we’re a community of 800 lawyers and 500 business services professionals across New York, Washington, DC, London, Frankfurt, and Brussels. We advise leading corporations, investment funds, and financial institutions on high-stakes M&A, securities, regulatory matters, real estate, and litigation. Our culture is grounded in our core values — excellence, integrity and collaboration — and is designed to foster continuous learning, meaningful mentorship, and lasting professional growth. We are firmly committed to pro bono service and social justice, building on a proud legacy in civil rights. Our inclusive talent strategy is a core part of our broader talent management efforts and we remain steadfast in fostering a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to grow, thrive, and become their best professional and personal selves. Our business services professionals are integral to the firm’s success, driving innovation, operational excellence and exceptional client service across all areas of the firm. We offer competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package, including comprehensive medical coverage, retirement plans and health and wellness initiatives designed to support your personal and professional wellbeing. We welcome passionate, driven individuals to join us, and be part of a team where you’ll be supported, inspired and empowered to build an exceptional career. Position Summary : The firm is seeking a motivated college student, grad student or recent graduate for a paid internship supporting our Legislative Research Attorney. This role is ideal for a student considering law librarianship, law school or a career as a paralegal, offering direct, hands-on exposure to how attorneys and legislative professionals track, analyze, and organize legal and regulatory developments to service clients. The intern will work closely with the Legislative Research Attorney and other staff and will gain practical experience with government publications, legal databases, AI tools, and document management systems used in a law firm practice. Duties & Responsibilities: Daily Federal Register and Congressional Record monitoring. Review and flag items relevant to the firm's clients and practice areas. Careful, daily reading provides hands on learning about the legislative and regulatory processes and allows for connections to be made beyond simple keyword alerts. Legislative and Regulatory transcript summaries. Using the latest legal AI tools, prepare and validate clear, concise summaries of bills, rules and congressional and agency hearing transcripts for use by attorneys and clients. Learn how to read and understand legislative and regulatory texts. Bill tagging in BGOV and StateNet. Accurately tag and categorize federal and state legislation within BGOV and StateNet tracking platforms. This work is detail-intensive but essential to keeping the firm's legislative tracking systems reliable. Legislative history (LH) folder construction in iManage. Assist with an ongoing project to build and organize legislative history folders in iManage, ensuring research materials and legislative histories are properly filed, searchable, and easily accessible to attorneys. Online legislative history pages. Help maintain and build out intranet pages to host legislative histories for significant bills. Create and update links back to the underlying materials in iManage. News and publication monitoring. Monitor business and legal news publications for developments relevant to the firm's clients and practice areas. Support the Legislative Research Attorney’s work in circulating relevant items to each team. Legal database research. Conduct research using legal and legislative databases to support ongoing monitoring projects. Education / Experience : Currently enrolled in an undergraduate degree or graduate degree program; students considering law librarianship, law school or a paralegal career are especially encouraged to apply. Interest in government, public policy, or law is a plus. Skills & Abilities : Strong reading comprehension and attention to detail. Prior exposure to complex legislative and regulatory texts is a plus. Excellent written communication skills, particularly the ability to summarize material clearly and concisely. Highly organized, reliable, and comfortable with repetitive, detail-oriented tasks that require sustained accuracy. Research capability, though no prior experience with BGOV, StateNet, or iManage is required; training will be provided. The actual salary offered will be based on a number of factors including but not limited to the qualifications of the applicant, years of relevant experience, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and if applicable, the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job. Washington DC Salary Range $20 - $20 USD

item.title: Design Selections Coordinator
item.description: Design & Selections Coordinator Sineath Construction Weaverville, North Carolina, United States Full-time 3 days ago $55,000 - $65,000 USD yearly Sineath Construction Weaverville, NC | Full-Time | In-Office About the Role Sineath Construction is looking for an organized, design-minded coordinator to support our Designer and Purchasing & Estimating team through the residential selection and pre-construction process. This role is a strong fit for an early-career interior designer who understands residential design and enjoys bringing structure to a project. You will help clients move from selections to approved specifications while keeping information, budgets, vendors, and deadlines aligned for the field team. What You'll Do Support the Lead Designer and Purchasing & Estimating team with residential finish selections. Coordinate client selection deadlines, approvals, specifications, and supporting documentation. Post and maintain accurate selection information in JobTread so clients, vendors, and field staff can easily follow the latest information. Communicate with clients, vendors, and trade partners through JobTread and other appropriate channels. Maintain selection reports and finish schedules for completeness, clarity, and team visibility. Track selection impacts on project budgets and update budget information after approvals. Coordinate selection-related purchase orders and help ensure materials are ordered and available when scheduled. Maintain vendor and trade partner information and support annual agreement and setup requirements. Assist with selection-related estimating tasks and variance purchase orders as needed. Track product rebate opportunities and help keep project records organized and current. Provide responsive client and partner communication throughout the selection process. What We're Looking For Degree or formal training in Interior Design, or approximately 2 years of relevant interior design experience. Residential design experience or a strong understanding of residential finishes, materials, and selections. Strong organizational and project coordination skills with excellent follow-through. Ability to manage multiple deadlines, details, vendors, and client requests at the same time. Clear, professional communication skills and a collaborative approach. Comfort working with budgets, specifications, and project documentation. Proficiency with Microsoft Office. Experience with JobTread, Bluebeam, Chief Architect, AutoCAD, SoftPlan, or similar design/project management software is a plus. Ability to work independently, make sound decisions, and ask for direction when needed. What Success Looks Like Selection information is accurate, current, and easy for clients and field staff to use. Client selections and approvals are completed by established deadlines. Selection-related orders are coordinated accurately and on time. Budget impacts and project documentation are kept current. Clients, vendors, designers, and field staff receive clear and timely communication. Compensation & Benefits Salary: $55,000-$65,000 annually , depending on experience. Full-time, in-person position with typical office hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. Medical Insurance : Eligible after 90 days Paid Time Off : 5 days/year (Years 1-2); 10 days/year after 2 years Sick Leave : 5 days/year 401(k) : Eligible after 1 year with company match (100% match on the first 3%; 50% on the next 2%) How to Apply Please submit your resume and a brief summary of your residential design or selections experience. Candidates with a portfolio or examples of residential design work may include those materials with their application. Weaverville, North Carolina, United States $55,000 - $65,000 USD yearly

item.title: Franklin County Election Canvasser
item.description: The Opportunity Down Home North Carolina (DHNC) seeks field canvassers in Franklin County to aid in our 2026 field campaigns. This year, Down Home members will endorse multiple candidates for office who align with our values and vision for a North Carolina that works for all working folks. Down Home is working to engage voters in our small towns this year to inform them about the upcoming elections, when, where, and how they can vote, and recruit more folks into our movement. Opportunities are available in the following counties: Ashe, Alamance, Cabarrus, Chatham, Franklin, Granville, Iredell, Johnson, Nash, Orange, Person, Pitt, Randolph, Rowan, Rockingham, Vance, Watauga, and Wilson. The ideal candidate is a people-person motivated to build a powerful multiracial base that wins changes for poor and working-class people in rural North Carolina. They have excellent listening skills, are team players and independent workers, and are aligned with Down Home's mission. The Work Have conversations with community members through door-to-door canvassing Participate in 4 to 6 canvasses per week Ensure that data and information collection are consistent and accurate Troubleshooting issues within the program Must be willing to work in a team-centered environment. Required Traits Excellent communication and listening skills: Can engage deeply with people they have just met. Be able to listen to community members and understand their concerns. Can build rapport quickly and is comfortable having relational conversations. Team player: Contribute to a growing and fast-paced team. Take directions well and be willing to offer feedback and suggestions to co-workers and management. Offer support to teammates and ask for help when needed. Independent worker: Be able to complete multiple canvass shifts a week. Meet deadlines and hit metric goals. Ensure that numbers are reported on time with data integrity at the top of mind. Attention to detail and be able to provide thoughtful solutions to problems that arise. Be able to work in a fast-paced environment where work areas are expected to change frequently. Mission alignment: Committed to the vision of a powerful, inclusive, rural, multiracial, working-class movement-building as a path towards liberation for all people. Is aligned with the idea that building power takes both election programs and long-term base-building and community investment. Compensation Compensation for this contract position is $22 hourly. Hours are flexible, with shifts available during the afternoon and evening. This role is not eligible for employee-sponsored benefits or healthcare. Applicants must be able and willing to travel regularly for work. How to Apply Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis if spots are available. We will still accept applications if this job description is posted on Down Home’s website (www.downhomenc.org).
