item.title: Research Associate U S Foreign Policy
item.description: $55,000 - $58,000 USD yearly Overview Founded in 1921, the Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is a leading nonprofit membership organization, research center, and publisher, with headquarters in New York, an office in Washington, DC, and programs nationwide. It is dedicated to increasing America's understanding of the world and contributing ideas to U.S. foreign policy. CFR's 5,000+ members are leaders in international affairs and foreign policy. CFR also publishes Foreign Affairs , the preeminent magazine on global issues, and provides up-to-date information about the world and U.S. foreign policy on its award-winning website, CFR.org. Position Summary CFR’s David Rockefeller Studies Program is one of the country’s largest foreign policy think tanks with a widely respected and influential research staff. The Studies Program’s aim is to advance the discussion of U.S. foreign policy and international affairs through its writing, publications, public outreach, and discussions. As part of the Studies Program, the research associate will support a variety of fellows and programs, including a senior fellow whose work focuses on international relations, foreign policy, and diplomatic history. This role encompasses both administrative and research support, with the balance between the two fluctuating based on fellow and program needs. This position is based in CFR’s Washington, DC, office on a hybrid basis. CFR defines hybrid status as working at least four days a week onsite, with Tuesday through Thursday considered institutional anchor days where all staff are required to be onsite. Essential Functions/Responsibilities Provide logistical and administrative support to fellows, including scheduling and calendar management, handling phone calls, and media requests, making travel arrangements, and drafting correspondence Coordinate events, including preparing invitations, making travel arrangements, corresponding with speakers, presiders, and participants, and providing logistical support for the event Conduct research and editing for articles, book chapters, and other publications Assist with budgeting, including tracking monthly income statements, monitoring grant information, potentially drafting grant reports and proposals, creating and updating Excel spreadsheets, and preparing vouchers for reimbursement Assist fellows with social media outreach, including website maintenance and posting and/or using social media platforms, as needed Support other fellows and departments, upon request Perform any other duties or tasks as assigned or required Minimum Qualifications Experience and Education Bachelor’s degree in a related field such as political science, history, or international relations or other related fields. Demonstrated interest in foreign policy studies, diplomatic history, or related fields Master’s degree preferred, but not required One or more years of related administrative and/or internship experience preferred Related Skills & Other Requirements Excellent research, writing, editing, and communication skills Strong organizational and time management skills, with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Ability to work independently while also collaborating effectively with others Ability to exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and manage sensitive information with discretion. Proficiency with Microsoft Office and other digital productivity tools, with strong online research and information-management skills Required Application Materials Please submit a résumé and cover letter stating your interest in the position. Compensation and Benefits The full-time annual compensation range for this position is $55,000 – $58,000, depending on experience. In addition to competitive salaries, the Council on Foreign Relations offers a benefits package that is among the best offered by nonprofit institutions today, including an award-winning health and wellness program, an on-site fitness center, and generous leave policies and health insurance programs. About CFR The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is committed to fostering a foreign policy community in the United States that is more representative of American society, recognizing that diverse backgrounds and perspectives contribute to broader, more informed participation in the foreign policy debate and lead to an enhanced understanding of the world and the United States’ role therein. To that end, CFR is dedicated to continuing to advance diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout its work and workplace by building a more diverse membership and staff, producing and dispensing thoughtful analysis on a broad range of foreign policy issues, and developing relevant, wide-reaching programming that also serves to expand the foreign policy talent pipeline to underrepresented populations. Assists customers at the counter and by telephone by responding to inquiries related to election records and the election procedures of the Clerk's Office. Assists with the development and delivery of training to precinct inspectors and local election officials, regarding election operations and standards. This includes assisting the Election Administrator in reviewing updates to election laws, regulations that may require an update to County Clerk’s election procedures and training materials for maintaining compliance. item.title: Director State Government Affairs Southeast Us
item.description: The Opportunity: Reporting to the Senior Director, State Government Affairs, as the Director of State Government Affairs, Southeast US you will be the key point of contact for government officials and stakeholders on state legislative and government policy matters that affect CSL Behring in the Southeast US region. You will have a proven ability to prioritize state activity and a demonstrated understanding of how government actions affect our patients and company operations. You will represent CSL and its facilities in the Southeast US region regarding public policy concerns and is responsible for state legislative and state regulatory policy interactions. You will collaborate with internal departments—such as market access, government reporting,reimbursement, corporate accounts, communications, marketing, sales, and our CSL Plasma business unit—will be essential, and the Director will be responsible for leading team efforts to assess and address policy issues impacting access to care and business operations in the assigned region. You will serve as the company liaison on policy matters with state patient advocacy organizations, trade associations, state medical societies and other groups with complementary policy goals. You will need to be based in the Southeast US region – TX, OK, AR, LA, MS, AL, KY, WV, VA, NC, SC, GA, FL. The Role: Represent CSL Behring and serve as key point of contact for public officials in the assignedregion, developing and maintaining relationships with members of state legislatures, committeestaff, administrative and regulatory officials, and identifying legislative and administrativechampions to advocate on issues affecting CSL Behring. Represent CSL Behring before variousstate legislative committees, agencies, etc. with regard to CSLB priorities. Provide legislative strategy and regulatory analysis in addition to political analysis and strategy.Draft legislation, provide technical corrections, and develop support for priorities. Must be ableto provide clear, relevant and succinct analysis and guidance to CSLB leadership and cross-functional teams. Represents our site operations throughout the Southeast region. Support the growth of CSL Plasma by identifying and developing public official champions andadvancing strong public policy that supports plasma donation. Assess and address legislativeand state regulatory issues affecting the CSL Plasma network. Support CSL’s product portfolio by creating and implementing action plans to advance statelegislative and regulatory initiatives that allow for access to CSLB therapies. Specifically,advocate for Medicaid policies to ensure patient access to CSL Behring therapies. Collaborationwith internal teams is essential, including market access, corporate accounts, reimbursement,contracting, communications, and others. Ability to lead cross-functional discussions, developand implement action plans, build grass roots support, and communicate status updates andresults to diverse stakeholders. Develop and execute relationship strategies for allies and patient advocacy organizations toadvance advocacy initiatives. Build and maintain grassroots coalitions, serving as key point ofcontact for policy and advocacy. Coordinate with other CSLB departments with responsibilitiesrelated to patient group outreach, and work with Policy, Advocacy, and Government Affairsteam on positioning CSL Behring’s state advocacy efforts, determining strategies and tactics inassigned states that support CSL Behring’s commitment to state advocacy. Prepare written summaries of legislation, government action, and analysis of issues for a rangeof audiences, including corporate leadership, patient advocacy organizations, and otherstakeholders. Develop concise and insightful presentations for patient advocacy organizationsand contribute articles as needed to corporate publications and communication channels.Ability to express major points in writing while translating complex topics into lay language isessential. Represent CSL Behring and participate in state affairs committees for trade associations whereCSL Behring has membership (PhRMA, BIO, state Biotech Associations, Chambers, etc.) Work and contribute as a team player by sharing best practices, communicating relevantinsights on issues and intelligence, leading special projects, and coordinating with teammembers to ensure CSL Behring State Government Affairs coverage of key meetings, events,and activities. Manage the business relationship and direct key activities of contract consultants in designatedstates and/or projects in order to advance our policy objectives. Your Skills & Abilities: Bachelor’s degree required (advanced degree preferred) in public policy, government, political science, or related field. 7+ years’ experience preferred, with demonstrated knowledge of the legislative and regulatory process, particularly in the Southeast US region. Previous experience in government affairs or state government is necessary, with state legislative experience desirable. Previous advocacy experience with pharmaceutical/biotech, trade associations or patient advocacy organizations is also highly desirable. Business acumen: understands the life sciences industry and how current and potential policies,trends and practices could affect the industry. Customer focus: able to establish and maintain effective relationships with internal and externalcustomers and gain their trust and respect. Timely decision-making: can make decisions in a timely manner, sometimes with incompleteinformation and under tight deadlines and pressure. Negotiation skills: Can negotiate skillfully in tough situations with both internal and externalgroups. Political Savvy. Priority setting and strong time management. Able to be a self-starter. Strong written communication and presentation skills. About CSL Behring CSL Behring is a global biotherapeutics leader driven by our promise to save lives. Focused on serving patients’ needs by using the latest technologies, we discover, develop and deliver innovative therapies for people living with conditions in the immunology, hematology, cardiovascular and metabolic, respiratory, and transplant therapeutic areas. We use three strategic scientific platforms of plasma fractionation, recombinant protein technology, and cell and gene therapy to support continued innovation and continually refine ways in which products can address unmet medical needs and help patients lead full lives. CSL Behring operates one of the world’s largest plasma collection networks, CSL Plasma. Our parent company, CSL, headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, employs 32,000 people, and delivers its lifesaving therapies to people in more than 100 countries. To learn more about CSL, CSL Behring, CSL Seqirus and CSL Vifor visit https://www.csl.com/ and CSL Plasma at https://www.cslplasma.com/ . Our Benefits For more information on CSL benefits visit How CSL Supports Your Well-being | CSL . You Belong at CSL At CSL, Inclusion and Belonging is at the core of our mission and who we are. It fuels our innovation day in and day out. By celebrating our differences and creating a culture of curiosity and empathy, we are able to better understand and connect with our patients and donors, foster strong relationships with our stakeholders, and sustain a diverse workforce that will move our company and industry into the future. To learn more about inclusion and belonging visit https://www.csl.com/careers/inclusion-and-belonging Equal Opportunity Employer CSL is an Equal Opportunity Employer. item.title: Legislative Director
item.description: Legislative Director Sierra Club Atlanta, Georgia, United States Full-time 3 days ago $86,000 - $86,000 USD yearly Job Title: Legislative Director Department: Georgia Chapter Location: Hybrid; must be able to travel to Atlanta daily Reports To: Chapter Director Supervises : Legislative Interns and Contract Lobbyists Context : At the Sierra Club, we believe in the power of interdependence. Together, we remain committed to the fight for a healthy climate built on a foundation of environmental, racial, economic, and gender justice – a future where all people benefit from a healthy, thriving planet and a direct connection to nature. As the climate crisis and deeply entrenched systemic racism all fuel injustice, we will continue to fight for a bold, transformational agenda that recognizes the interconnectedness between our planet, our humanity, and our future. By recognizing that our destinies are tied, we continue to name that all things are fundamentally connected, and the overlap between ecology, race, gender, and representative government will move to either advance our collective humanity or to oppress it. Sierra Club has close to 700 staff across the country and a network of 64 local chapters that are led and fueled by thousands of volunteers. We are also proud to be a unionized employer, with three labor unions representing more than half of our employees. Scope: The Legislative Director builds the Chapter’s power and influence through delivery of legislative advocacy efforts. Maintains governmental and political contacts, evaluates legislation, makes strategic recommendations related to legislation, and lobbies at the state and local level. This is a hybrid position that requires frequent in-person meetings as well as in-state travel. Job activities include but are not limited to: Legislative Strategy. Plans, coordinates, and implements the Chapter’s legislative strategies as approved by the Chapter Legislative Committee. Writes and implements work plans for legislative campaigns and coordinates with staff and volunteers to develop campaign goals and tactics that will deliver policy wins in alignment with the Chapter’s priorities. Collects and maintains legislative data, evaluates legislative strategies, reports campaign outcomes to the Chapter Director, and makes recommendations on adjusting organizing strategy as needed. Legislative Lobbying. Builds and maintains relationships with elected officials and legislative staff. Coordinates with groups and partners in order to rally support/opposition for bills, initiatives, laws, or resolutions. Monitors, studies, and researches proposed legislation to determine possible effects on the environment and makes appropriate recommendations to the Legislative Committee. Confers with legislators and officials to emphasize merits or weaknesses of specific bills to influence passage, defeat, or amendment of measure, or introduction of legislation that defend and advance environmental protection. In consultation with the Legislative Chair and contract lobbyist, prepares for legislative hearings and meetings. Ensures compliance with state and federal law and files lobbyist reports. Policy Messaging & Communications. Works with Sierra Club staff and coalition partners to develop a consistent, clear state policy and legislative message that is being communicated to the public, relevant communities, and stakeholders. Tracks legislative proceedings to ensure proper messaging and leads rapid response strategy. Write legislative briefs and works with communications staff to develop one-pagers, talking points, and policy toolkits. Grassroots Mobilization. Manages and implements legislative mobilization efforts including but not limited to: indirect lobbying, direct-to-target messaging, coalition events, SMS, and phonebanking. Designs and facilitates legislative training for volunteers and manages in-district lobbying volunteer programs. Plans and coordinates meetings between members and elected officials to discuss legislative issues and proposals and allow for officials to hear and consider member concerns. Convenes coalition spaces, meetings, and events in coordination with partners to plan mobilization opportunities, activations, and events Representation. Represents Sierra Club to elected officials, the public, in coalition meetings, legislative meetings, and events. Serves as Sierra Club spokesperson to media outlets and promotes volunteer and partner organization media exposure as needed. Collaboration with Committees. Writes legislative scorecard with Legislative Committee, works with Political Committee on endorsements, and serves as staff lead for Coordinated Campaign work. Is staff support on committees (Legislative, Clean Energy, Transportation, Wildlands, and Political) Manage Legislative Staff. Hires, manages and supports legislative staff, including: contract lobbyists and legislative interns. Manages hiring processes and executes contracts in alignment with the chapter's budget and priorities. Establishes performance objectives and expectations, and evaluates accomplishments and effectiveness. Tracks grant deliverables, progress and performance and, when necessary, helps course correct and respond to challenges. Advance Georgia Chapter’s Cultural Transformation Goals. Supports implementation of the Chapter's efforts to cultivate an environment that benefits from a broad coalition of identities reflecting the richness of cultures across Georgia. Seeks and creates opportunities to affirm the belonging of partners and members through political and legislative work. Miscellaneous. Travel is required for staff meetings, volunteer group meetings, statewide legislative functions, and other meetings and events deemed relevant to the duties of the job. Meetings and other work outside of regular business hours, including weekends and evenings is required. Heavier workloads may occur as a result of deadlines and during peak activity periods. The successful candidate must demonstrate the following skills, experience and competencies: Subject matter expertise. Substantial subject matter expertise in environmental policy, political science, or both. Prior experience and effectiveness in lobbying. Clear understanding and knowledge of the legislative and political process. Team Leadership. Prior experience and/or demonstrated ability in developing, training, and coaching teams of staff and volunteers in achieving shared goals. Experience in organizational conflict resolution and committed communication skills. Ability to address and resolve conflicts within the organization effectively, fostering a positive and collaborative work environment. Relevant experience. Must have experience working as a lobbyist. Must have experience with Georgia state-wide and/or local politics. Strong analytical skills. Ability and willingness to conduct strategic outreach. Successful candidates will show a strong desire to engage in collaboration, conduct outreach, and build networks throughout the organization and the state. Strong communication skills, both verbal and written. Successful candidates will demonstrate the ability to communicate effectively and clearly both verbally and in writing. Committed to evolution. You are committed to continuously deepening and evolving your own understanding of systems of oppression through study, openness, and humility. And you easily recognize your own relationship to privilege and power, examining and shifting your behaviors as appropriate. Uplifting and additive . You see mistakes as opportunities for growth; problems as catalysts for solutions, and inspire others along the journey. You carry a constructive approach, can-do attitude, a sense of humor, and authentic kindness wherever you go. The strongest candidates will also demonstrate the following skills, experience and competencies: A deep knowledge and understanding of Georgia’s unique legislative and political landscape. Experience and a deep understanding of the rules, laws, and guidelines as they relate to political and lobbying work in Georgia, both advocacy and electoral. Can recognize where work needs to be done and fill the gaps. Self-motivated; can work independently as well as part of a team. Working knowledge of operations, budget management, and grant funding. Fast learner who can quickly absorb, distill, and communicate to diverse audiences new and often complex information $86,000 - $86,000 a year Compensation and Benefits The salary for this position is $86,000 annually. The Sierra Club offers a competitive salary package commensurate with skills and experience plus excellent benefits that include medical, dental, and vision coverage, and a retirement savings 401(k) plan. This is a category 4, exempt, non-represented, supervisory position. Sierra Club values the expertise and talents of foreign nationals. Sierra Club sponsors both nonimmigrant and immigrant visas when certain criteria are met, based on immigration laws and organizational needs. item.title: Chief Legislative Affairs Division
item.description: Duties This position is located under the Office of Public and Governmental Affairs, Legislative Affairs Division in Washington, DC. The major duties of the Chief, Legislative Affairs Division position include, but are not limited to, the following: Ensure that congressional inquiries are responded to timely and accurately while always keeping their sights on the frequent sensitivities surrounding these and the associated requirements that may come from the Department Advise Bureau executives on a legislative strategy to accomplish Bureau goals and objectives and develops and promotes a legislative liaison program to accomplish those goals. Developing and implement nationwide legislative affairs strategies, activities, policies and programs and representing the Bureau in meetings and discussions with the member of Congress, their staff and top level offices from the Department of Justice and ATF. Stay aboard of newly proposed or enacted legislation affecting Bureau programs and servs as technical advisor to the AD and DAD, PGA and the Bureau Director and Deputy Director, providing authoriative analysis regarding new or revised legislatoin and intiatives having natioal or internatonal implications. Develop and maintain effective working relationships with other top Deparment and Bureau officials and keeps abreast of problems of a politcally sensiteve nature, areas of special or urgent Congressional interest, and any developments or problems relating to Bureau programs and budgetary needs Summary The primary purpose of this position is to serve as the Chief of the Legislative Affairs Division, Office of Public and Governmental Affairs (PGA) for the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives(ATF) and is responsible for developing, implementing, and directing the legislative affairs program, ensuring harmonious relationships with officials from the Department of Justice, Members of Congress, their staffs, and those committees that oversee the work and resources of the Bureau. Requirements Conditions of employment The requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement. Must be U.S. Citizen or National Selective Service registration is required for males born on, or after, December 31st 1959. Those not registered should have an approved exemption on file. May be required to serve a one-year probationary period. Suitable for Federal employment determined by background investigation. You must meet all applicable time-in-grade requirements by the closing of this announcement. Financial Disclosure: If selected, you may be required to disclose financial information in accordance with DOJ and Federal ethics guidelines. MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of ATF's mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. To accomplish these objectives, the mobility plan will facilitate the movement of employees through special short-term assignments or permanent reassignments throughout the Bureau. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process. This is a non-bargaining unit position. Qualifications To qualify for this position at the GS-15 grade level, candidates must also have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-14 by the closing date of this announcement. Specialized experience is demonstrated experience, which has equipped the applicant with the particular knowledge, skills and abilities to perform successfully the duties of this position. Experience must be in the normal line of progression or must be related to the work of the position advertised and must be reflected in resume. Specialized experience must include all of: Apply laws and regulations governing law enforcement, industry operations and other local, state and federal statutes; AND Develops and implements a federal legislative affairs strategies, activities, policies and programs; AND Prepares and provides official material to Congress regarding Bureau goals, objectives, and the effectiveness of programs; AND Establish parameters for assuring timely and quality completion of work assignments related to legislative affairs activities; AND Responds to congressional inquiries. Your resume must support your responses to the application questionnaire and the qualification requirements. Failure to do so may result in an ineligible rating. See the Required Documents section for important notes about what must be included in your resume. Education Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone. No substitution of education for experience is permitted. Additional information Additional selections may be made from this announcement. A one-year probationary period is required for new supervisors and managers. As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you will be serving in a position in Schedule Policy/Career of the excepted service. You will obtain competitive status after two years of service in this position [if applicable]. Your employment in this position will be at-will. Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB) appeals of adverse actions concerning performance, discipline, and other matters arising under chapters 23, 43, and 75 of title 5, United States Code will not be available to an individual serving in this position. Prohibitions on prohibited personnel practices will not be enforced by the Office of Special Counsel but rather by a DOJ-wide mechanism. Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. Notice to Prospective Employees of Ethical Obligations from ATF's Human Resources Operations Division. Please click on the following link to read important information. To receive selection priority for this position, you must: Meet CTAP or ICTAP eligibility criteria; Be rated well-qualified for the position with a score of 85 or above based on the competencies listed above; and Submit the appropriate documentation to support your CTAP or ICTAP eligibility. item.title: Assistant Professor Of Political Science Public Administration
item.description: Current University of Arkansas System employees, including student employees and graduate assistants, need to log in to Workday via MyApps.Microsoft.com, then access Find Jobs from the Workday search bar to view and apply for open positions. Students at all University of Arkansas institutions will view open positions and apply within Workday by searching for “Find Jobs for Students.” University of Arkansas, Fayetteville students will view open positions and apply within Workday by searching for “Find Student Jobs at UAF.” All Job Postings will close at 12:01 a.m. CT on the specified Closing Date (if designated). If you close the browser or exit your application prior to submitting, the application process will be saved as a draft. You will be able to access and complete the application through “My Draft Applications” located on your Candidate Home page. Closing Date: Type of Position: Faculty - Tenure/Tenure Track No Job Type: Regular Yes Institution Name: University of Arkansas, Fayetteville Founded in 1871, the University of Arkansas is a land grant institution, classified by the Carnegie Foundation among the nation’s top 2 percent of universities with the highest level of research activity. The University of Arkansas works to advance the state and build a better world through education, research, and outreach by providing transformational opportunities and skills, fostering a welcoming climate, and nurturing creativity, discovery, and the spread of new ideas and innovations. The University of Arkansas campus is located in Fayetteville, a welcoming community ranked as one of the best places to live in the U.S. The growing region surrounding Fayetteville is home to numerous Fortune 500 companies and one of the nation’s strongest economies. Northwest Arkansas is also quickly gaining a national reputation for its focus on the arts and overall quality of life. As an employer, the University of Arkansas offers a vibrant work environment and a workplace culture that promotes a healthy work-life balance. The benefits package includes university contributions to health, dental, life and disability insurance, tuition waivers for employees and their families, 12 official holidays, immediate leave accrual, and a choice of retirement programs with university contributions ranging from 5 to 10% of employee salary. Below you will find the details for the position including any supplementary documentation and questions, you should review before applying for the opening. If you have a disability and need assistance with the hiring process, please submit a request via the Disability Accommodations | OEOC | University of Arkansas (uark.edu) : Request an Accommodation. Appli­cants are required to submit a request for each position of which they have applied. For general application assistance or if you have questions about a job posting, please contact Human Resources at 479.575.5351. Department: Department of Political Sciences Summary of Job Duties: The Department of Political Science in the Fulbright College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Arkansas invites applications for a tenure-track assistant professor position in public administration, public policy, and nonprofit studies, beginning in August 2027. This is a standard nine-month faculty appointment. The successful candidate will serve as a core faculty member in the Master of Public Administration and Nonprofit Studies (MPA) program. The department’s standard teaching load is two courses per semester, for a total of four courses per academic year. The successful candidate will be expected to teach graduate courses that support the MPA program and introductory level undergraduate courses. This is an in-person position. Regular, reliable, and non-disruptive attendance is an essential job duty, as is the ability to create and maintain collegial, harmonious working relationships with others. About the Department: The Department of Political Science consists of 22 full-time faculty. For more information about our department, please visit https://fulbright.uark.edu/departments/political-science. Duties will include: • 40% Teaching or Professional Performance • 40% Research/Scholarly and/or Creative Activities • 20% Academic Service Activities Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications: A Ph.D. in political science, public administration, public policy, nonprofit studies, or a closely related field conferred by the start date of employment from an accredited institution of higher education Potential to contribute to high-quality scholarship in public administration, public policy, nonprofit studies, or a closely related area Ability to teach at least one graduate course in public administration, public policy, or nonprofit studies that supports the MPA program Ability to teach introductory level undergraduate courses in the Department of Political Science Preferred Qualifications: Evidence of a coherent and productive research agenda, including peer-reviewed publications or a strong pipeline of scholarly work Evidence of effective college-level teaching Ability to teach two or more of the MPA course areas identified above Experience or demonstrated ability to mentor students Research and teaching interests that complement and broaden the strengths of the Department of Political Science and the MPA program Qualification Equivalencies: Additional Information: This position is a Designated Research Position and is regulated by the Arkansas Research Education Protection Act of 2025 . Prior to issuance of an offer of employment, the University is required to request and obtain additional information about an applicant’s background and, if required, conduct an additional review of that background information. Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications. Required Documents to Apply: Cover Letter/Letter of Application, Curriculum Vitae, List of three Professional References (name, email, business title), Other (see special instructions for details) Proof of Veteran Status Recruitment Contact Information: Dr. Geoboo Song, gbsong@uark.edu All application materials must be uploaded to the University of Arkansas System Career Site https://uasys.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/UASYS Please do not send to listed recruitment contact. Special Instructions to Applicants: APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS Completed applications received by October 8, 2026, will be assured full consideration. Late applications will be reviewed as necessary to fill the position. For additional inquiries, please contact the search committee chair, Dr. Geoboo Song, at gbsong@uark.edu. Applicants must submit: 1) A curriculum vitae; 2) A cover letter explaining their interest in the position and how their research and teaching meet the advertised qualifications; 3) A research statement; a teaching statement that identifies the MPA courses and an appropriate 20000-level undergraduate course they would be prepared to teach and includes evidence of teaching effectiveness; 4) One representative writing sample; 5) A list of three professional references (name, title, institutional affiliation, email address, and phone number). Letters of recommendation will not be required as part of the initial application and will be requested only for candidates selected for interviews. Review of applications will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. Pre-employment Screening Requirements: Criminal Background Check, Sex Offender Registry The University of Arkansas is committed to providing a safe campus community. We conduct background checks for applicants being considered for employment. Background checks include a criminal background check and a sex offender registry check. For certain positions, there may also be a financial (credit) background check, a Motor Vehicle Registry (MVR) check, and/or drug screening. Required checks are identified in the position listing. A criminal conviction or arrest pending adjudication or adverse financial history information alone shall not disqualify an applicant in the absence of a relationship to the requirements of the position. Background check information will be used in a confidential, non-discriminatory manner consistent with state and federal law. The University of Arkansas seeks to attract, develop and retain high quality faculty, staff and administrators that consistently display practices and behaviors to advance a culture that embeds equal opportunity, educational excellence and unparalleled access for all. The University of Arkansas is an equal opportunity institution. The University does not discriminate in its education programs or activities (including in admission and employment) on the basis of any category or status protected by law, including age, race, color, national origin, disability, religion, protected veteran status, military service, genetic information, sex, sexual preference, or pregnancy. Questions or concerns about the application of Title IX, which prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex, may be sent to the University’s Title IX Coordinator and to the U.S. Department of Education Office for Civil Rights. Persons must have proof of legal authority to work in the United States on the first day of employment. All Application information is subject to public disclosure under the Arkansas Freedom of Information Act. Constant Physical Activity: N/A Frequent Physical Activity: N/A Occasional Physical Activity: N/A Benefits Eligible: Yes

item.title: Federal Government Affairs Manager Rise
item.description: Federal Government Affairs Manager (RISE) Croplife America Arlington, Virginia, United States Full-time 1 day ago Location: Arlington, Virginia Position Type: Full-Time Travel: Some travel is required for industry conferences and other stakeholder engagements. Reports To: Executive Director RISE (Responsible Industry for a Sound Environment), a trade association representing the specialty (non-agricultural) pesticide and fertilizer industry, is seeking a full-time Federal Government Affairs Manager based in Arlington, Virginia, near our nation’s capital. The successful candidate must register as a federal lobbyist. As a member of the public affairs team, this position will strengthen RISE’s federal advocacy presence on Capitol Hill and help ensure the association is a force multiplier for the industry. This role offers direct exposure to congressional policymaking and the opportunity to help shape advocacy outcomes for an industry with a broad national footprint. Responsibilities include supporting federal advocacy strategies that integrate grassroots engagement and communications to engage members, allies, congressional offices, policymakers, and other stakeholders. Responsibilities: Coordinate with the RISE team to develop and implement effective grassroots engagement strategies that mobilize members and allies on federal issues. With the Executive Director, help lead RISE’s congressional advocacy initiatives by cultivating relationships with national partner associations, key congressional offices, and committee staff, and positioning RISE as a subject matter expert on issues affecting its membership. Help lead educational meetings with congressional staff on behalf of the Pesticide Policy Coalition, focusing on foundational pesticide regulation education and the benefits of specialty pesticides and fertilizers. Support the development and execution of RISE’s federal appropriations strategy, including building congressional resource materials, identifying key House and Senate targets, and supporting a national campaign. Track congressional developments, hearings, markups, member priorities, committee activity, and relevant political dynamics to help inform RISE’s advocacy strategy. Assist in the development and delivery of public policy presentations and updates on behalf of RISE at industry conferences. Assist in composing and distributing informative and compelling correspondence, testimony, policy positions, grassroots alerts, congressional briefing materials, meeting notes, follow-up summaries, reports, toolkits, and background materials to support engagement on priority issues. Prepare for, participate in, and follow up on meetings with Members of Congress, congressional staff, committee staff, coalition partners, and member company representatives. Assist with planning and execution of RISE fly-ins, including member preparation, scheduling, materials development, congressional meeting logistics, and follow-up. Collaborate closely with RISE colleagues and members to advance federal advocacy, grassroots engagement, and communications initiatives. Participate in political fundraisers, industry events, coalition meetings, and other stakeholder engagements outside normal business hours, as needed. Other responsibilities as assigned. Education and Work Experience: Minimum of a BA/BS degree in political science, communications, public relations, environmental science, or a similar field. Minimum of 3 years of experience in public policy, legislative affairs, government affairs, or advocacy is required; at least 1 year of experience working in Congress, with a congressional committee, or in a congressional-facing advocacy role is preferred Additional Qualifications: Ability to self-start projects and independently manage assignments while meeting established timelines. Drive to become a subject matter expert on legislation and regulations broadly impacting the specialty pesticide and fertilizer industry. Ability to monitor federal legislative activity, identify emerging congressional trends, and summarize implications for members and internal stakeholders. Ability to proactively develop and maintain key relationships with congressional offices, committee staff, members, allies, RISE contract lobbyists, coalitions, grassroots stakeholders, teammates, and other stakeholders. Ability to build trust and work effectively with congressional offices, committee staff, coalition partners, and stakeholders across the political spectrum. Ability to exercise political acumen in assessing congressional dynamics, stakeholder interests, and opportunities for effective Hill engagement. Embodies flexibility, sound judgment, and discretion. Excellent written and oral communication skills, including strong writing, proofreading, editing, and the ability to distill complex or technical information into concise, effective, and influential materials. Experience tracking legislation and summarizing policy proposals. Familiarity with the U.S. pesticide regulatory system and current policy issues is preferred but not required. Proficiency in Microsoft Office and legislative tracking tools. Arlington, Virginia, United States

item.title: Usa Director Government Affairs And Public Policy
item.description: Position Summary... What you'll do... Role summary: The (USA) Director, Government Affairs and Public Policy leads strategic engagement to align and execute public policy initiatives with organizational objectives. This role shapes high-impact messaging, manages complex reputational risks, and fosters collaborative partnerships across markets and industries. By integrating policy insights with business strategy, the director advises leadership on emerging risks and opportunities, drives proactive external storytelling, and guides cross-functional teams through scenario planning and decision-making processes. The position requires expertise in advocacy, public policy and public affairs to influence outcomes and support long-term organizational goals. About the team: The State & Local Government Relations team represents Walmart before state and local governments, advancing public policy priorities and managing emerging issues. Collaborating across the business, the team monitors and shapes legislation and regulations impacting stores, associates, customers, and operations. They engage with governors, legislators, local officials, and stakeholders to develop state-specific strategies and clear advocacy. Team members anticipate risks and opportunities, exercise sound political judgment, and build strong relationships that support Walmart’s mission to serve customers and communities effectively. This position will be based in New York state, with a preference to be located in Albany. What you'll do: Develop and execute Walmart’s state government affairs strategy in New York and an additional state, advancing legislative, regulatory, and public policy priorities. Represent Walmart before governors’ offices, legislatures, attorneys general, regulatory and economic development agencies, and local officials. Build trusted relationships with policymakers, regulators, trade associations, and key stakeholders. Monitor and engage on legislation, regulations, and emerging political issues affecting Walmart’s business. Lead advocacy strategies, coalition efforts, and direct policymaker engagement. Anticipate political and policy risks and provide strategic counsel to leadership. Translate complex business issues into compelling policy arguments, briefings, testimony, and executive recommendations What you'll bring: At least 10 years experience in policy analysis, public policy advocacy, and regulatory compliance within complex environments. Proven ability to lead strategic communication and public affairs initiatives across multiple stakeholder groups. Strong skills in stakeholder engagement, coalition building, and influencing decision-making at senior levels. Expertise in developing and executing comprehensive communication and crisis response plans. Demonstrated capability to manage projects, including budgeting, scheduling, and risk mitigation. Proficiency in coaching teams on negotiation, storytelling, and conflict resolution in public policy contexts. Ability to integrate strategic foresight and business insights to shape policy and reputational outcomes. At Walmart, we offer competitive pay as well as performance-based bonus awards and other great benefits for a happier mind, body, and wallet. Health benefits include medical, vision and dental coverage. Financial benefits include 401(k), stock purchase and company-paid life insurance. Paid time off benefits include PTO (including sick leave), parental leave, family care leave, bereavement, jury duty, and voting. Other benefits include short-term and long-term disability, company discounts, Military Leave Pay, adoption and surrogacy expense reimbursement, and more. You will also receive PTO and/or PPTO that can be used for vacation, sick leave, holidays, or other purposes. The amount you receive depends on your job classification and length of employment. It will meet or exceed the requirements of paid sick leave laws, where applicable. For information about PTO, see https://one.walmart.com/notices . Live Better U is a Walmart-paid education benefit program for full-time and part-time associates in Walmart and Sam's Club facilities. Programs range from high school completion to bachelor's degrees, including English Language Learning and short-form certificates. Tuition, books, and fees are completely paid for by Walmart. Eligibility requirements apply to some benefits and may depend on your job classification and length of employment. Benefits are subject to change and may be subject to a specific plan or program terms. For information about benefits and eligibility, see One.Walmart . The annual salary range for this position is $110,000.00 - $220,000.00 Additional compensation includes annual or quarterly performance bonuses. Additional compensation for certain positions may also include : - Stock ㅤ ㅤ ㅤ ㅤ ‎ Minimum Qualifications... Outlined below are the required minimum qualifications for this position. If none are listed, there are no minimum qualifications. Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Policy, Economics, Communications, or related area and 8 years’ experience in government relations, public policy research, legislative affairs, regulatory analysis, or related area OR 10 years’ experience in government relations, public policy research, legislative affairs, regulatory analysis, or related area Preferred Qualifications... Outlined below are the optional preferred qualifications for this position. If none are listed, there are no preferred qualifications. Advanced graduate degree; experience leading large-scale/national or multi‑market government affairs initiatives within the region or area of expertise., People management experience. Primary Location... 141 WASHINGTON AVE EXTENSION, WALMART ALBANY, NY 12205-0000, United States of America Walmart and its subsidiaries are committed to maintaining a drug-free workplace and has a no tolerance policy regarding the use of illegal drugs and alcohol on the job. This policy applies to all employees and aims to create a safe and productive work environment.

item.title: U S Public Policy Advocacy Intern
item.description: Our team members are at the heart of everything we do. At Cencora, we are united in our responsibility to create healthier futures, and every person here is essential to us being able to deliver on that purpose. If you want to make a difference at the center of health, come join our innovative company and help us improve the lives of people and animals everywhere. Apply today! The U.S. Public Policy & Advocacy Summer Intern will support the U.S. Public Policy & Advocacy team through policy research, advocacy project support, project coordination, knowledge management, and development of reusable team materials. This internship is designed as a structured, development-focused 10-week experience that provides exposure to healthcare policy, federal and state government affairs, legislative and regulatory processes, advocacy strategy, corporate stakeholder engagement, and the pharmaceutical supply chain. This role will support meaningful, project-based work aligned to real team priorities while building the intern's skills in research, writing, synthesis, professional communication, organization, data validation, project tracking, and cross-functional collaboration. The role is intended to support Cencora's early talent pipeline and align with future workforce planning and talent development opportunities. The intern will contribute to discrete, supervised projects involving advocacy resources, state-level footprint materials, shared resource organization, policy research, meeting preparation, and team infrastructure initiatives. Projects will be designed to encourage critical thinking, problem solving, collaboration, and development of tangible deliverables that support business objectives. The intern will maintain a project and accomplishment log throughout the internship and prepare a final presentation summarizing completed work, key deliverables, skills developed, and overall business impact. Job Requirements The Summer Intern, U.S. Public Policy & Advocacy will be responsible for: Conducting research on federal and state policy issues, healthcare legislation, regulatory developments, congressional activity, trade association activity, and industry trends relevant to Cencora's policy and advocacy priorities. Drafting concise internal summaries, background documents, one-pagers, biographies, briefing materials, meeting preparation documents, and presentation content for internal stakeholders under manager guidance. Supporting state-level advocacy resource development by validating data, organizing information, identifying gaps or inconsistencies, and coordinating with internal stakeholders as needed. Assisting with maintenance of team trackers, shared resources, project logs, templates, repositories, meeting materials, and process documentation. Supporting organization and maintenance of shared team folders, onboarding materials, project resources, knowledge repositories, and other business-critical documentation. Attending selected congressional hearings, industry briefings, internal meetings, team calls, and advocacy-related events, and preparing concise summaries of key takeaways. Supporting planning and coordination for meetings, office visits, fly-ins, briefings, advocacy activities, and special projects as assigned. Collaborating with colleagues across Public Policy, Federal Advocacy, State Advocacy, PAC, Corporate Responsibility, Marketing, and other business functions on assigned initiatives. Maintaining a task and project log that documents assignments, deliverables, accomplishments, and skills developed throughout the internship. Completing a final presentation summarizing project outcomes, business impact, professional development experiences, and recommendations for future work. Required Knowledge Basic understanding of U.S. government, public policy, political processes, legislative affairs, healthcare policy, business, communications, or related subject matter. Interest in healthcare, government affairs, advocacy, public policy, legislative affairs, stakeholder engagement, or the pharmaceutical supply chain. Ability to conduct research, analyze information, and synthesize findings into clear, concise written materials. Understanding of professional written and verbal communication, including proofreading, accuracy, and audience awareness. Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing high-quality work products. Understanding of confidentiality, professionalism, discretion, and appropriate handling of sensitive information. Familiarity with Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Teams, and SharePoint. Ability to organize information in a clear and accessible manner. Ability to work independently on assigned projects while collaborating effectively with team members. Ability to manage multiple priorities, adapt to changing business needs, and communicate proactively regarding workload and project status. Required Experience / Relevant Coursework Candidates should be currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in a relevant field, including but not limited to: Political Science Public Policy Government Public Administration Health Policy Healthcare Administration Communications Journalism Business Administration Economics International Affairs Law or Pre-Law Data Analytics Public Affairs Related liberal arts, policy, business, or healthcare fields Preferred Coursework or Experience Coursework in U.S. government, legislative process, public policy, healthcare policy, political science, economics, communications, business, research methods, public administration, law, or data analysis. Experience conducting research, writing summaries, preparing presentations, organizing data, drafting reports, or supporting team projects. Experience using Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, or SharePoint through academic, volunteer, internship, work, or student organization activities. Experience in policy, advocacy, government, communications, nonprofit, healthcare, business, legal, administrative, or research-related settings preferred but not required. Experience collaborating in team environments, managing deadlines, organizing information, and communicating updates effectively. item.description: Current University of Arkansas System employees, including student employees and graduate assistants, need to log in to Workday via MyApps.Microsoft.com, then access Find Jobs from the Workday search bar to view and apply for open positions. Students at all University of Arkansas institutions will view open positions and apply within Workday by searching for “Find Jobs for Students.” University of Arkansas, Fayetteville students will view open positions and apply within Workday by searching for “Find Student Jobs at UAF.” All Job Postings will close at 12:01 a.m. CT on the specified Closing Date (if designated). If you close the browser or exit your application prior to submitting, the application process will be saved as a draft. You will be able to access and complete the application through “My Draft Applications” located on your Candidate Home page. Closing Date: Type of Position: Faculty - Tenure/Tenure Track No Job Type: Regular Yes Institution Name: University of Arkansas, Fayetteville Founded in 1871, the University of Arkansas is a land grant institution, classified by the Carnegie Foundation among the nation’s top 2 percent of universities with the highest level of research activity. The University of Arkansas works to advance the state and build a better world through education, research, and outreach by providing transformational opportunities and skills, fostering a welcoming climate, and nurturing creativity, discovery, and the spread of new ideas and innovations. The University of Arkansas campus is located in Fayetteville, a welcoming community ranked as one of the best places to live in the U.S. The growing region surrounding Fayetteville is home to numerous Fortune 500 companies and one of the nation’s strongest economies. Northwest Arkansas is also quickly gaining a national reputation for its focus on the arts and overall quality of life. As an employer, the University of Arkansas offers a vibrant work environment and a workplace culture that promotes a healthy work-life balance. The benefits package includes university contributions to health, dental, life and disability insurance, tuition waivers for employees and their families, 12 official holidays, immediate leave accrual, and a choice of retirement programs with university contributions ranging from 5 to 10% of employee salary. Below you will find the details for the position including any supplementary documentation and questions, you should review before applying for the opening. If you have a disability and need assistance with the hiring process, please submit a request via the Disability Accommodations | OEOC | University of Arkansas (uark.edu) : Request an Accommodation. Appli­cants are required to submit a request for each position of which they have applied. For general application assistance or if you have questions about a job posting, please contact Human Resources at 479.575.5351. Department: Department of Political Sciences https://politicalscience.uark.edu Summary of Job Duties: The Department of Political Science in the Fulbright College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Arkansas invites applications for a tenure-track assistant professor position in Political Science to start in August 2027. We are particularly interested in candidates whose research and teaching interests lie in the field of public law, with preferred specializations in jurisprudence, immigration law, family law, environmental law, or political theory. The expected teaching load for the position will be two courses per semester. Duties will include teaching undergraduate and graduate courses, performing research in their area of expertise, and contributing to the service needs of the department. Faculty hired in this position will have an opportunity to be a part of Fulbright College’s multidisciplinary Democracy as a Public Good cluster hire at the University of Arkansas. Through its Democracy as a Public Good Initiative, the College will advance the University’s land-grant mission by expanding capacity to generate knowledge that informs public understanding, contributes to policy and practice, and connects Arkansas to national and international conversations about societal good. Building on existing campus expertise in issues ranging from norms of democratic communication, free speech, media ethics and literacy, humanitarian governance and civil society, risks that AI poses to democratic governance, immigration, and public law, new faculty members participating in the cluster will advance their research agendas through mentoring and opportunities for collaboration—both with other scholars and with communities in the state—that may result in peer-reviewed publications, external funding, and new approaches to the pressing challenges that democracy faces. The successful candidate for this position will have an opportunity to join a community of scholars committed to confronting major issues, generating new knowledge, and providing research-based solutions that investigate and strengthen democratic culture for people living in Arkansas and beyond. This is an in-person position. Most university classes are offered face-to-face, and extensive in-person engagement in such activities as office hours, student advising, and departmental, college, and university committee meetings is essential to advancing student success and departmental effectiveness. Regular, reliable, and non-disruptive attendance is an essential job duty, as is the ability to create and maintain collegial, harmonious working relationships with others. About the Department: The Department of Political Science currently consists of 22 full-time faculty and is committed to strengthening its faculty, student body, and curriculum. For more information about our department, please visit https://fulbright.uark.edu/departments/political-science. Duties will include: • 40% Teaching or Professional Performance • 40% Research/Scholarly and/or Creative Activities • 20% Academic Service Activities Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications: A Ph.D. degree in Political Science or a closely related field from an accredited institution of higher education conferred by August 2027 from an accredited institution of higher education A record of publication or submission of research in reputable scholarly outlets Demonstrated evidence of effective teaching in teaching evaluations, sample syllabi, or a teaching portfolio Demonstrated ability to teach an undergraduate Introduction to American Government course Demonstrated ability to teach undergraduate coursework in at least two areas of public law A well-defined and coherent research agenda Preferred Qualifications: A strong and active research agenda that is well-grounded in political or legal theory, backed by advanced analytical, methodological, and empirical skills and focuses on some aspects of public law Demonstrated potential for publishing in top-tier outlets Demonstrated commitment to undergraduate and graduate education and a willingness to contribute to the department’s existing strengths in teaching and research Demonstrated ability to teach undergraduate coursework in political theory Demonstrated potential to secure external grant funding Demonstrated potential for national and international scholarly reputation Qualification Equivalencies: Additional Information: This position is a Designated Research Position and is regulated by the Arkansas Research Education Protection Act of 2025 . Prior to issuance of an offer of employment, the University is required to request and obtain additional information about an applicant’s background and, if required, conduct an additional review of that background information. Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications. Required Documents to Apply: Cover Letter/Letter of Application, Curriculum Vitae, List of three Professional References (name, email, business title), Other (see special instructions for details) Proof of Veteran Status Recruitment Contact Information: Dr. Andrew Dowdle, professor, adowdle@uark.edu All application materials must be uploaded to the University of Arkansas System Career Site https://uasys.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/UASYS Please do not send to listed recruitment contact. Special Instructions to Applicants: Completed applications received by October 12, 2026, will be assured full consideration. Late applications will be reviewed as necessary to fill the position. For additional inquiries, please contact the search committee chair, Andrew Dowdle, at adowdle@uark.edu. To complete the application, candidates will need to submit: (1) a cover letter indicating interest and qualifications; (2) a current curriculum vita; (3) a research statement; (4) a teaching statement describing approach to instruction, assessment of learning, and means of including students from different backgrounds and with different learning abilities; (5) evidence of teaching effectiveness, including teaching evaluations (when available) demonstrating excellence in instruction; (6) unofficial graduate transcripts; (7) one single-authored writing sample; and (8) names of three academic references (only finalists will be asked to submit letters of recommendation). Review of applications will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. Pre-employment Screening Requirements: Criminal Background Check, Sex Offender Registry The University of Arkansas is committed to providing a safe campus community. We conduct background checks for applicants being considered for employment. Background checks include a criminal background check and a sex offender registry check. For certain positions, there may also be a financial (credit) background check, a Motor Vehicle Registry (MVR) check, and/or drug screening. Required checks are identified in the position listing. item.description: Are you looking to work on current and emerging policy issues? Do you want to apply your education and experience to help government agencies improve the way they develop and implement regulations, policies, and programs? Our Regulatory, Policy, and Economics Portfolio has over 30 years of experience supporting the design, implementation, and improvement of federal programs for key clients including the Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Transportation, Department of Homeland Security, Department of Labor, Department of Interior, and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Join our multidisciplinary team of regulatory specialists, policy analysts, economists, and attorneys. We combine legal, policy, economic, and scientific research and analysis to solve unique public policy challenges through innovative, accurate, timely, and high-quality products and services. Our dynamic work environment involves working on multiple projects simultaneously, supporting a variety of federal clients, and providing a wide range of support services. This entry-level full-time position will be hybrid from our Reston, VA headquarters. Job Responsibilities: Participating in short- and long-term engagements to support federal clients whose responsibilities are to develop policies and craft regulations that implement the desired policy, explain the rationale of the rulemaking to interested parties; and implement the regulatory requirements Supporting federal agency efforts to transparently manage and analyze public comments received on proposed agency rules Assist in drafting and editing documents related to federal agency rulemakings Immersing oneself rapidly in varied projects for multiple clients Providing verbal and written progress updates to project staff Synthesizing information from rulemaking documents, literature, and other technical reports Assist in developing recommendations through collecting and analyzing both qualitative and quantitative data Drafting reports and presentations Interacting with clients to discuss ICF’s analysis Basic Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in public policy, government, environmental science, natural or physical science, political science, or related subjects U.S. Citizenship is required per federal contract requirements Ability to obtain and maintain a government security clearance Preferred Qualifications: Understanding of the federal rulemaking process Ability to obtain and maintain a moderate-level government security clearance Strong analytical and organizational skills are essential Ability to prioritize and work on multiple projects under strict deadlines in a fast-paced environment Excellent written and oral communications skills Detail-oriented and team-oriented approach Proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint) and Adobe; and Time management strategies Bot and Third-Party Applications Please note that this application must be submitted directly by the applicant for consideration. Failure to do so may result in the application being excluded for consideration . We combine unmatched expertise with cutting-edge technology to help clients solve their most complex challenges, navigate change, and shape the future. We can only solve the world's toughest challenges by building a workplace that allows everyone to thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer . Together, our employees are empowered to share their expertise and collaborate with others to achieve personal and professional goals. For more information, please read our EEO policy. item.title: Head Of Spectrum Management Government Affairs
item.description: Our client is developing a fully commercial next-generation GPS/PNT system to provide significant performance, security and reliability improvements for its users. The system will provide users with better accuracy, faster Time to First Fix (TTFF), solid anti-jam and anti-spoof capabilities, and will support US Government position and timing service resiliency along with next-generation commercial applications like drone delivery, self-driving cars, urban air mobility, and augmented reality. The $260B annual GNSS Hardware, Software and Data Services market is ripe for disruption and improvement, and the company intends to lead that revolution with its commercial infrastructure and services. The Position Our client is currently seeking a Full-Time Head of Spectrum Management & Government Affairs at its Herndon, Virginia location to secure and protect the spectrum its constellation depends on, lead its engagement with U.S. Government stakeholders, and advance the company’s role in ensuring resilient Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) for critical infrastructure and national security. Spectrum is the company’s wireless real estate, and this role owns it. You will own, build out and execute the roadmap that secures its radionavigation-satellite service (RNSS) and supporting allocations across domestic and international regulators, coordinate with incumbent GNSS and other operators to avoid harmful interference, and defend its rights over the life of the constellation. The work is both technical and political: you will be as comfortable in an interference analysis or an ITU coordination meeting as in a conversation with an agency lead or a Congressional office. Alongside spectrum, this senior role will drive the company’s broader regulatory and policy strategy, guide export control compliance, and build coalitions across federal agencies, Congress, industry, and international forums. As a pivotal leader in a fast-growing venture, you will directly shape how its commercial PNT system integrates with national security priorities and commercial markets. The position is hybrid, based in Herndon with regular access to Washington, DC, and includes occasional domestic and international travel as required. We’ll Expect You To… Lead Spectrum Management (75%) Own the company’s spectrum strategy and multi-year roadmap, securing, protecting, and expanding its RNSS, TT&C, feeder link, and inter-satellite link spectrum across domestic and international bodies. Lead ITU satellite network filings and coordination under the Radio Regulations, including advance publication, coordination requests, notification, bringing into use, and NGSO milestone obligations, working through the responsible notifying administrations. Negotiate and document coordination agreements with incumbent GNSS system operators, other satellite networks, and terrestrial users, and resolve interference concerns before they become disputes. Lead or direct interference and compatibility analyses (PFD, EPFD, aggregate interference, and protection criteria) that support filings, coordination positions, and regulatory submissions. Manage FCC satellite licensing and U.S. market access (Part 25 applications, modifications, and related filings) and coordinate with NTIA and the IRAC on federal band sharing. Secure earth station licensing and landing rights for the company’s ground network and service markets, country by country. Represent the company in World Radiocommunication Conference (WRC) preparation, ITU-R study groups and working parties, and U.S. preparatory processes, shaping agenda items that affect RNSS and PNT. Partner with Space Systems and Signals engineering so payload, emission, and system design decisions stay consistent with filed and coordinated parameters. Monitor for harmful interference, and manage outside spectrum counsel, consultants, and filing budgets. Lead Government Affairs & Policy (25%) Serve as the company’s primary liaison to the civil PNT policy community, including the National Coordination Office (NCO) for PNT, DOT, DHS/CISA, NIST, NASA, and the policy offices of the FCC and NTIA, to position commercial LEO PNT as a recognized complement to GPS. Participate in interagency working groups, federal advisory bodies, and public-private forums shaping civil PNT resilience and complementary PNT policy, and provide technical input to National PNT Strategy updates, Federal Radionavigation Plan revisions, and related civil policy processes. Represent the company in a focused set of standards bodies, trade associations, and industry coalitions where participation directly supports its spectrum and regulatory objectives. Track federal policy and regulatory developments affecting civil PNT, critical infrastructure timing, and commercial space, and translate them into concise internal guidance for the executive team and engineering. Oversee regulatory compliance for space operations and exports, including launch licensing, UN space object registration, and ITAR/EAR compliance (TAAs, DSP-5s, and company-wide export training), in coordination with outside counsel.
